- The needed capabilities or obtainable contributions are recovered far enough for this use.
- A changed encompassing condition and a constituent limitation reveal their effects.
- The correction addresses the diagnosed difficulty and preserves applicable rights and authority.
- The result states what is explained or corrected and what performance remains unestablished.

### CGOV.16:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Anti-pattern | What fails | Useful correction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The vertical is a list of departments. | Reporting or supplier relations do not explain constituent performance. | Follow the chosen action through its actual encompassing work. |
| A correct constituent is assumed to establish the whole. | Eligibility, interpretation or coordination conditions can still fail. | Carry the whole's conditions into the constituent operation. |
| Training covers each operation only in isolation. | The performer cannot coordinate them under the real governing conditions. | Practise or obtain the contribution within the needed combination. |
| Every diagnosed failure triggers governance redesign. | A local execution or capability repair is displaced by a larger project. | Select the smallest supported correction that restores the required performance. |

### CGOV.16:9 - Consequences

A governance problem can be assigned to the contribution that needs repair. Teams can distinguish missing knowledge, inadequate execution, incompatible combinations and infeasible demands. They can also divide support work more rationally while retaining the parts that the corporate procedure requires its participants to perform.

The method adds explanation where isolated task descriptions fail. Its scope can remain small; following every possible dependency would obscure the condition that changes the next action.

### CGOV.16:10 - Architectural Rationale

The same work can enact methods at several levels of composition. Its constituent actions receive conditions from their encompassing use and make that use performable. Treating this only as a sequence of outputs misses what is being done through what at the chosen moment.

Corporate rights, participation rules and conditions for an institutional act to take effect constrain the constituent/encompassing relation. Recovering that relation helps authorized participants perform or correct the corporate act.

### CGOV.16:11 - SoTA-Echoing

The [UK private-company model articles](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/model-articles-for-private-companies-limited-by-shares/model-articles-for-private-companies-limited-by-shares) make participation, quorum and conflict conditions distinguishable from counting. They provide a concrete institutional anchor; the examples use their own supplied rules.

The [IIA Three Lines statement](https://www.theiia.org/globalassets/site/resources/statements-of-position/tlm_assurance_advice_support_effective_gov_en.pdf) distinguishes interacting governance, management and assurance contributions. This helps avoid treating their organizational arrangement as one Method vertical. The constituent/encompassing analysis here is a conceptual synthesis through B.1.5.EW, not a claim that the IIA statement prescribes this method.

### CGOV.16:12 - Relations

B.1.5.EW supplies the general recovery method. B.5.RC helps reconstruct an unfamiliar constituent operation; B.1.5.RS helps when a constituent is to be replaced. C.32.MWA is useful when different Method, Work, subject and organizational structures must be related.

CGOV.1–CGOV.3 supply relevant matter, rights and authority conditions. CGOV.6–CGOV.12 contribute the particular conflict, information, control, assurance, decision or protection work being examined; applying all of them is not a prerequisite.

C.32.MWA.PP compares materially different arrangements for performing and supporting the connected methods when needed. Use CGOV.14 when a governing arrangement must change through its applicable procedure. A recurrent capability or transmission difficulty can inform development or cultural work through HCD and CGOV.17.

### CGOV.16:End

## CGOV.17 - Deliberately Continue and Change Corporate-Governance Culture

> **Type:** Method
> **Status:** Stable

### CGOV.17:1 - Problem frame

Use this pattern when corporate participants need to preserve, transmit or change a shared way of governing. A board may retain its papers and procedure while newcomers cannot challenge a proposal's assumptions. A committee may know how to raise an exception but stop doing so when challenge is discouraged. A professional association may distribute guidance without knowing which practices recipients can use.

Start with the corporate contribution that must remain obtainable and the participants who need it. Recover how it is actually performed, locate a consequential gap, and choose how to sustain or renew the practice.

The first result can be a qualified account of the practice, a supported decision to continue it, or a proposed change. When implementation is assigned, continue through the receiving participants' use. Claims that a practice persists or improves governance need observations of those further consequences.

Here, governance culture concerns shared ways of working and the processes through which people or organizations transmit, recognize, select, retain or lose them. Use an adequate available practice directly. A single person's difficulty within a stable arrangement can use the relevant development method without a wider cultural-change project.

### CGOV.17:2 - Problem

A code, training session or stored board pack can help transmit a practice, but each leaves open what recipients can do with it. They may reproduce the form while losing the reasoning that made it useful. They may understand the method but lack access to information, time for the work or conditions for expressing an independent judgement.

Corporate authority introduces another difficulty. A specialist can supply an analysis while a director retains a duty to deliberate; an association can recommend a procedure while the company retains its own adoption powers. Substituting one contribution for the other can preserve visible activity while losing the required corporate work.

Calling every such failure “culture” conceals the repair. Repeating training cannot restore inaccessible information. Publishing a new code cannot establish performance. Replacing the whole arrangement can discard useful practice that remained available.

### CGOV.17:3 - Forces

Continuity supports reliable corporate work, while changing participants, circumstances and methods can require renewal. Informal ways of working can preserve useful judgement or protect habits that suppress challenge.

Capabilities can be distributed among directors, staff, specialists and tools, but corporate responsibilities and powers constrain that distribution. Confidentiality can limit observation and teaching material. Existing evidence can justify a useful correction even when a broad cultural or causal claim remains unanswered.

### CGOV.17:4 - Solution

Follow a needed corporate contribution through its performance, means of acquisition and conditions of continued use. Change the part that prevents participants from obtaining it.

#### CGOV.17:4.1 - Bound the practice and the question

Name the corporation or practitioner population, the work concerned and the period relevant to the question. Identify what participants need to obtain: for example, an informed investment judgement, a usable control exception or an account of an unfulfilled undertaking.

Distinguish the requested result. An explanation of what is currently practiced can finish without an intervention. A continuity assignment needs a way to keep the contribution available. An assignment to introduce another method needs the corresponding change and receiving use.

Recover the applicable responsibilities, powers and information conditions. Use established answers from CGOV.1–CGOV.3 and CGOV.8. If the observation or proposed action requires permission, obtain it through the applicable arrangement. Bound a claim when information is unavailable.

#### CGOV.17:4.2 - Recover the practice that participants actually use

Use available cases, explanations and observations to recover the operations and their results. Identify how participants encountered the method, which aspects they learned or obtained from others, and what they used in the receiving matter.

Keep the cultural claims distinct. Distribution shows that material was sent. A demonstrated receiving use can show a transferred operation. Continued use within an observed period supports a claim about that period. Selection or rejection of a method needs its own basis. C.36 supplies these distinctions.

The observations need only answer the current question. A known departure can justify arranging a replacement contributor without a study of the entire board's culture. A broader claim about persistence or consequences may remain open.

#### CGOV.17:4.3 - Locate the missing contribution and its cause far enough to act

Follow the corporate task to the first consequential gap. C.36.RP, Sustain and Renew Shared Ways of Working, supplies the general method.

Ask whether participants can obtain the input, recognize when the method applies, perform or obtain the operation, interpret its result and use it in the corporate work. Distinguish a capability gap from a condition that prevents an available capability from being expressed.

For example, a director may understand a cash forecast but receive it after the decision. A new committee member may have the information yet be unable to interpret a control exception. A capable member may stop questioning proposals when the chair repeatedly excludes those questions. These situations call respectively for information provision, learning or capable support, and repair of the working arrangement.

Recover constituent work where it matters. A correct calculation can still be unusable in deliberation if its assumption is lost in the summary. CGOV.16 helps locate that connection and retain the contributions that remain sound.

#### CGOV.17:4.4 - Arrange the suitable means of continuation or renewal

Choose a repair that answers the found gap. An explanation, demonstration, practice with feedback, obtainable specialist or improved information service can each be appropriate.

Determine which understanding the corporate participant must retain and which operation can be supplied by others. A director may receive specialist analysis while needing to recognize its assumptions and exercise the judgement assigned to the director. People, AI and tools can supply permitted contributions; the governing rules determine any non-transferable participation or decision duty.

Use the relevant capability-development or explanation method when acquisition is needed. Preserve enough of the reasoning and conditions for the receiving use. A participant who must adapt a method needs more than a completed answer to copy.

When the method itself must change, CGOV.15 helps compare and maintain the alternatives. When the governing arrangement must change, use CGOV.14. A known repair within existing powers can proceed without another corporate act. If an act is required, use its applicable procedure.

C.11.DUA governs additional inquiry. Include the effort of access, confidentiality arrangements, performance, interpretation and displaced corporate work when deciding whether a proposed study is worth doing. Preserve applicable duties while limiting optional inquiry to the decision it can change.

#### CGOV.17:4.5 - Carry the contribution into receiving work

When implementation is assigned, make the selected support or learning available and use the method in the receiving matter. Give participants the information and participation conditions needed for that work.

Observe the contribution relevant to the original difficulty. Can newcomers recover the assumption and use it in deliberation? Does an exception reach the person able to respond? Does an eligible participant actually take part in the collective act?

Distinguish performance with assistance from unaided performance when that difference matters. Assistance can remain part of the intended arrangement. A useful distributed practice does not require every participant to perform every specialist operation.

Return a remaining failure to its cause or required contribution. A plan or completed teaching event is an earlier result than receiving use. Receiving use is in turn narrower than demonstrated persistence or improved corporate outcomes.

#### CGOV.17:4.6 - Retain the means of use and reconsider them when needed

Keep the explanation, examples, access and capable help that later participants need. Use permitted material and protect information whose disclosure is restricted. A sanitized case may teach a reasoning operation while real work still requires authorized access to the company-specific information.

Provide a practical route for the next succession, changed question or failed use to expose a new gap. Retain useful alternatives where conditions differ. A candidate method can deserve preservation for later exploration without being introduced into a live corporate decision.

End the current work when its account, continuation decision or assigned implementation is supplied. Use C.36 for any later claim about transmission, retention, loss or cultural consequences beyond the observed scope.

### CGOV.17:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### CGOV.17:5.1 - Retain judgement across board succession

This is a constructed case. CairnCo appoints three new directors. Its rules require directors to take part in deliberation and the board's investment decisions. They may obtain specialist analysis, and the chair may arrange induction and preparation support under existing powers. All directors have access to the relevant papers.

The board's guide instructs readers to identify assumptions that could change an investment judgement. An outgoing director usually did this aloud. New directors can repeat the instruction but, in an induction case, do not connect a proposed facility's first deliveries with the expiry of the customer's current contract.

The gap concerns use of the reasoning operation. The chair arranges a demonstration of how an assumption changes the proposed judgement. The newcomers then examine a different proposal with the company's analyst available for calculations.

In the next board matter, the directors identify that the forecast relies on renewal of an unconfirmed customer contract. They ask for the consequence of non-renewal and use the analyst's answer in deliberation. The board makes its decision under the existing procedure.

Within this constructed case, the receiving use shows the operation being performed with specialist assistance. The board retains the explanation, an authorized route to the analyst and a way to revisit the operation during later induction. Longer persistence and commercial benefit remain separate questions.

If the directors instead understood the operation but received the contract information too late, the suitable repair would concern information provision. Repeating the demonstration would leave that failure unresolved.

#### CGOV.17:5.2 - Distinguish distributed guidance from shared practice

In this constructed case, a professional association distributes a revised procedure for reporting control exceptions. Eight companies download it. The association has permission to examine two companies' uses; confidentiality prevents observation in the others.

In the first company, an exception reaches the audit committee through an existing authorized channel and changes the requested follow-up. In the second, the supplied rules require this type of exception to reach the audit committee. Staff complete the form but send it only to the executive whose activity is questioned. An independent reporting channel is already authorized but staff cannot access it.

The immediate repair in the second company is access to the authorized channel, followed by its use. Adopting another code or repeating the form-filling lesson does not supply that access.

The association can describe distribution to eight companies and the observed uses in two. It cannot infer the other six companies' practice or an improvement in their performance. A company seeking local adoption still applies its own governing conditions.

### CGOV.17:6 - Bias-Annotation

Visible documents and training attendance are easier to observe than everyday judgement. Observations may also favour participants willing or permitted to report. Preserve the scope of what is known.

Continuity can protect valuable practice or exclusionary habits. Compare whose contribution is retained or suppressed and how that affects the corporation and applicable rights. Do not equate popularity inside a dominant group with adequacy for the corporate work.

### CGOV.17:7 - Conformance Checklist

- The practice, participants, receiving work and relevant period are identified.
- The account distinguishes available material, capability, receiving use and any stronger cultural claim.
- The repair answers a consequential gap in operation or its conditions.
- Responsibility, decision power, information access and confidentiality remain respected under their applicable basis.
- The selected learning, support or change reaches the result the assignment requires.
- Any claim of persistence or improved consequences stays within its observations.

### CGOV.17:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Failure in the situation | Repair |
| --- | --- |
| Training attendance is used as evidence that directors can use the method. | Examine the operation in the receiving work when that claim matters. |
| A capability problem is assumed while the necessary information is inaccessible. | Restore the information contribution. |
| A specialist's competent analysis is treated as the director's required judgement. | Preserve the supplied analysis and the director's separate participation. |
| A code revision is reported as adoption across the profession. | Distinguish publication, distribution and the uses actually observed. |
| Every continuity problem starts a whole-company culture programme. | Locate the missing contribution and make the smallest sufficient repair. |

### CGOV.17:9 - Consequences

A corporation can retain ways of governing through changes of participants without relying on unexplained habit. The method also makes room for replacing a practice whose conditions or consequences no longer fit.

Learning, support and observation consume resources, and confidential work can limit the available evidence. The method permits a useful bounded continuation while keeping stronger claims open. It can also reveal that the needed change concerns access or authority rather than capability.

### CGOV.17:10 - Architectural Rationale

Governance culture involves both the availability of methods and their use under corporate relations. A stored procedure can preserve an operation's description while losing the capability or permission needed to perform it. Conversely, a change in access can restore performance without changing the method.

C.36 supplies the cultural-relation distinctions; C.36.RP supplies the general recovery of shared ways of working. Corporate application must also preserve the difference between specialist support, the participant's own judgement and the collective act, together with the governing rights and information conditions. Those relations determine where a repair belongs.

CGOV.15 maintains method choices and their applicability. This method concerns how those choices become and remain usable among participants. Observed use can return to that comparison when it exposes a limitation or useful variation.

### CGOV.17:11 - SoTA-Echoing

The [FRC Corporate Governance Code Guidance](https://www.frc.org.uk/library/standards-codes-policy/corporate-governance/corporate-governance-code-guidance/), especially paragraphs 19–24, 170–180 and 232–236, connects governance practice with behaviour, development, actual discussion and conditions for challenge. Adopt those practical questions within the guidance's scope; recommendation alone does not demonstrate cultural or commercial effects.

C.36 distinguishes transmission, receiving use, selection, retention and loss; C.36.RP sustains obtainable methods through suitable learning, access and distributed contributions. C.11.DUA keeps further inquiry proportional to the receiving decision. The cases are constructed applications, not observations of actual companies.

Reconsider the arrangement when succession, changed information conditions, new methods or observed failures change what participants can obtain and use. A dated code or source revision can prompt that question when its content matters.

### CGOV.17:12 - Relations

CGOV.1–CGOV.3 and CGOV.8 supply unresolved corporate basis, powers and information conditions. CGOV.6 and CGOV.7 address a relevant conflict or eligibility problem. CGOV.16 helps recover the constituent contributions needed for the corporate work.

CGOV.15 supplies a method or comparison when alternatives are needed; observations from receiving use can revise its applicability. CGOV.14 changes an arrangement when that is required, and CGOV.11 supplies the method for a required corporate decision.

Use C.36 and C.36.RP for the cultural and continuity work, and the relevant capability-development and explanation methods for acquisition. CGOV.13 can follow a corporate undertaking to provide the selected continuation.

### CGOV.17:End

# Customization and Productization Management Principles Framework Readme

## Practical entries

Bring the question you are actually trying to answer. These entries are selected examples, not a catalogue or a coverage boundary. If none fits, search the Table of Contents or enter a pattern directly. You can ask an assisting agent: “Explain this and give me your comments in ordinary language, without framework jargon.”

### CUST-ENTRY-DELIVERY - Turn a successful delivery into an obtainable method

- **Situation:** A service works when its author is present, but another prepared team cannot yet repeat it.
- **Question:** Which work, preparation and help must become available for the next delivery?
- **First useful result or blocker:** A constructed delivery method with an attainable receiving performance, or the exact missing capability, permission or support.
- **Start with:** [CUST.6](#cust6---establish-repeatable-deployment-and-service-delivery).
- **Stop or return:** Retain explicit assisted provision when it fits; return a false family assumption to CUST.3.

### CUST-ENTRY-CHANGE - Improve the common offering while current customers continue

- **Situation:** A shared change affects installed configurations, accepted meanings or support promises.
- **Question:** How can the affected customers obtain a valid continuation?
- **First useful result or blocker:** A compatible extension, transition, coexistence or retained arrangement with its work and authority, or the unresolved receiving result.
- **Start with:** [CUST.8](#cust8---change-the-offering-family-with-compatible-customer-transitions).
- **Stop or return:** Do not widen the change beyond its supported conditions. Preserve unaffected service and obtain the missing contribution.

### CUST-ENTRY-GROWTH - Grow without hiding repeated invention

- **Situation:** Several customers want related adaptations, and common development appears attractive.
- **Question:** What can we share, how will it be delivered and what burden follows?
- **First useful result or blocker:** A supportable answer connecting what can be shared, an obtainable delivery method and the full resource comparison, or the condition preventing it. A successful local case can remain local.
- **Start with:** [CUST.1](#cust1---manage-client-variation-and-develop-repeatable-offerings), connecting the family in CUST.3, delivery in CUST.6 and resource comparison in CUST.7.
- **Stop or return:** Use an adequate existing configuration directly. Narrow or stop the affected promise when capability, permission, resources or current obligations defeat it.

## Use the whole Method or a sufficient part

**Start with the supported offering and the actual customer result. Recover their consequential differences, then construct a compatible local and shared continuation.** Productization can produce a repeatable service or reusable contribution; it does not require every local adaptation to become a common product.

The intended reader manages a product, service, customer delivery, implementation practice or another undertaking with continuing customer commitments. Use the large CUST.1 Method when the customer case and future offering must be developed together. Use a smaller Method when the current problem is already bounded. A supported configuration needs no new productization programme.

Read the [Architectural Reference](#custreference1---field-and-use) for the field, connections and limits. [Using FPF Library](../../USING-FPF.md) explains how to obtain supplying frameworks. Perform the work with the required professional capabilities and permissions.

# Customization and Productization Management Principles Framework Architectural Reference

## CUST.Reference:1 - Field and Use

Customization and Productization Management concerns the continuing development of customer-specific results and repeatable offerings together. Its object is the arrangement of customer commitments, local differences, common contributions, provision and support. A product manager, service lead, delivery lead or another responsible practitioner uses it when a decision about one of these changes the others.

The recurring difficulty is not merely excessive customization. A valuable local adaptation can expose a useful common capability; a common release can damage an existing customer's result; a standard delivery method can depend on unprovided expert work. The useful gain is to make these consequences decidable and their continuation obtainable.

A customer result and a repeatable provider contribution are distinct. A deployment can work for its recipient while depending on exceptional effort, unavailable data or an undocumented specialist. Conversely, a reusable component can be technically sound while leaving the customer's operating change, training or support unresolved. CUST connects these two results without requiring both to succeed in every case.

An **offering** is the result or contribution offered to someone, together with its conditions of provision. A **family** contains offerings or configurations whose common basis, permitted differences and support can be explained together. A **delta** is a consequential difference from the chosen supported basis; it may concern work or obligations as well as an artifact. A **local residue** is a contribution deliberately retained for a particular case rather than admitted to the common family.

“Customer” includes the recipient or party whose work is served; payer, user and beneficiary may differ. Public and nonprofit provision can be valuable without a positive margin on each recipient. Its commitments still require actual resources and support.

The intended practitioner can investigate the customer's work, recover the supported offering and obtain the relevant professional contributions. CUST supplies management Methods at several useful scales.

## CUST.Reference:2 - Boundaries and the Meaning of the Name

The chosen name joins two directions of work. **Customization** develops a fitting result from a supported basis under actual customer conditions. **Productization** develops a sufficiently defined, repeatable offering or reusable contribution from variable work. The second direction can produce an assisted service, a delivery method or a restricted family; it need not produce a standalone artifact or remove every specialist.

**Management** identifies the question of making commitments, contributions, resources and revisions fit together. It does not name a mandatory department. The same person may perform compatible contributions, and a small team may use the full Method.

| Neighboring field or label | Contribution retained | Boundary of CUST |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Marketing | Customer results, meaningful offers, programmes, inquiry and promise–execution alignment. | CUST constructs and governs the relation between actual deltas, a repeatable family, delivery capability and continuing obligations. It does not redefine customer or market inquiry. |
| Systems Engineering | Product and platform families, supported use paths, integrated offering/provider concepts, compatibility and transition. | CUST uses these engineered results in the wider customer and resource decision. It does not replace technical realization or its qualification. |
| Operations Management | Actual operating capacity, variability, coordination and feasible service commitments. | CUST explains which local and shared work the operating arrangement must provide. |
| Management Accounting | Customer and product economics over time. | CUST supplies the complete provision boundary and alternatives; accounting supplies their qualified economic treatment. |
| Implementation Facilitation | Inquiry into implementation difficulties, support construction and actual transfer. | CUST adds the connected local/shared receiving decisions, including whether field experience should change a repeatable offering. |
| Semantic Integration Engineering | Meaning, correspondence and permitted receiving use across contexts. | CUST uses the qualified meanings to distinguish consequential deltas. |

Several alternative names remain useful for their own scopes. *Productization Management* foregrounds conversion into common provision but can hide the continuing legitimate local result. *Customization Management* can hide the reverse movement into a changed common family. *Mass Customization* supplies a strong line of solution-space development, robust process design and choice navigation, including services; CUST also admits useful local-only provision, non-repeatable residue and refusal. *Solution Business* includes wider commercial and relational questions. *Product and Service Management* is broader than this field. *Forward-Deployed Engineering* names one practice arrangement, not the whole field.

This combined name is a local synthesis.

## CUST.Reference:3 - Methods and Their Connections

The framework is a repertoire of related Methods, including a large immediately usable composition. CUST.1 supplies the whole customer-case continuation. CUST.2 through CUST.8 can be used independently when their problem is already bounded; they also supply developed contributions to CUST.1. Their numbers are addresses, not a compulsory production sequence.

| Current difficulty | Contribution and receiving connection |
| --- | --- |
| The request is expressed only as features | CUST.2 reconstructs consequential differences from the supported basis and their dependencies. CUST.1 uses them to compare complete continuations. |
| A useful local result might become common | CUST.3 constructs the family, its invariants, variation and exclusions. It can receive CUST.5 field evidence without treating a successful case as admission. |
| The family exists but selection or delivery timing is unclear | CUST.4 makes the customer's choice meaningful and places common and customer-dependent work. The result constrains actual operating capacity and support. |
| A decision-changing premise remains unknown | CUST.5 obtains a bounded local and shared answer. The answer can narrow a promise, exclude a member or end further inquiry. |
| Repetition depends on its author | CUST.6 constructs a usable method, preparation and support, then performs the receiving connection. It can reveal a false family assumption rather than a documentation defect. |
| Growth appears attractive but its burden is unclear | CUST.7 compares complete provision over a stated population and period. The result can change the family, assistance, differentiation point or growth decision. |
| A common change affects current users | CUST.8 constructs compatible customer continuations and an attainable transition. Its result changes the family and its support burden. |

Three relations help the reader use this arrangement accurately.

**Method composition** connects ways of obtaining component results into a way of obtaining the whole result. In ongoing work, a selected action can enact contributions to that whole at the same time: while the field team resolves an ambiguous input, it may be performing part of the current customer delivery and part of constructing the repeatable family. The whole constrains that action: the team may use the customer's material for authorized local work but cannot place it in a partner package when that receiving purpose is not permitted. The local action must then produce a qualified conclusion or an independently permitted example, not a copied dataset.

**Use of an earlier result** concerns something already obtained. A qualified semantic mapping, accounting comparison or compatibility result can be consumed without rerunning the supplying Method. Its meaning, conditions and remaining uncertainty travel with it. Changing those conditions reopens the affected use.

**A repertoire** makes methods available for different situations. It does not require all of them on every occasion. CUST.7 can justify continued bespoke work with no common development. CUST.8 can manage retirement without a new field probe. A supported configuration can finish the customer case without a new family.

The large Method remains useful even when its operations are familiar. It provides the joins, simultaneous conditions, branch choices and returns that would otherwise have to be invented for each case. A list of supplying patterns does not supply those joins.

## CUST.Reference:4 - Make the Whole Arrangement Work

Customer usefulness, common reuse, current service, resources and permission constrain one arrangement. Individually plausible contributions can be impossible together. A customer may accept an outcome target, engineering may produce a working component and accounting may show an attractive unit cost, while the only qualified specialist is already committed elsewhere. The joined promise remains unavailable until that conflict is resolved.

CUST.1:4.3 explains how to make the relevant decisions governable. Recover the needed contributions, actual decision authority and timing, then join the answers before a consequential promise. A shared role holder may supply several answers; a consequential conflict can require separate judgement.

Meaning differences should be treated where they affect work. The customer's “active” status, the provider's supported calculation, the deployment team's observed records and the commercial promise may differ. Use the full Semantic Integration methods when an adequate correspondence is missing. Separating those viewpoints is a beginning; explain the correspondence needed to use each result.

Two recurring loops have different receiving results. The **customer loop** obtains a useful local continuation, including preparation, assistance, acceptance and support. The **common-development loop** constructs and qualifies a reusable contribution and makes it obtainable in later provision. They exchange deltas and evidence, but either can end without the other succeeding. A valuable local adaptation may remain local; negative field evidence may improve the common boundary even when local deployment stops.

The common contribution can take several forms: a parameter, a component, a supported profile, a delivery method, an assisted service or an integrated offering. These are alternatives with different work and support, not steps in a maturity ladder. A case may combine them. CUST.2 keeps the decision axes distinct; CUST.3 builds a family; CUST.4 selects and supplies a fitting configuration.

Before promising scale, specify what grows and what mechanism changes the burden. More customers, more variants, more throughput, a longer support horizon and more delivery partners present different questions. Common preparation may lower repeated effort after enough uses while increasing initial work. A partner may add ordinary delivery capacity while leaving central expert work unchanged. CUST.7 keeps these claims separate and comparable.

## CUST.Reference:5 - Connected Worked Applications

These examples are constructed to show operations and consequential choices.

### CUST.Reference:5.1 - A monthly analytical service with a private deployment

A provider offers a hosted monthly eligibility report. A new customer needs private hosting, enterprise sign-on, a different meaning of “active,” a local report layout and urgent support. Treating this as one customization price would conceal several different problems.

CUST.1 first places the existing provision beside the customer's required result. CUST.2 separates the linked deltas. Enterprise sign-on may fit a supported adapter. Private hosting changes preparation and support. The meaning of “active” requires an explained correspondence or a distinct profile. The report layout may remain a local service. Urgent support changes capacity even if no code changes.

CUST.3 constructs a candidate family: a common monthly reporting purpose, qualified input meanings, an ordinary hosted member and a private member with stated access and preparation conditions. A disconnected immediate-response service is excluded because its operation and support do not fit the common basis.

CUST.4 helps the customer choose between the hosted and private members and makes the necessary customer work visible. CUST.5 investigates the unsettled access condition through a permitted bounded attempt. The field result supports local use with assistance, but reveals manual input correction that was absent from the shared-delivery claim.

CUST.6 reconstructs that correction, makes input interpretation and exception handling explicit, and supplies preparation and scheduled help. Another prepared performer then performs the work. If extra author assistance remains necessary, the provider can retain it as explicit assisted provision, improve the method or narrow the supported class.

CUST.7 compares the full work at the intended volume. Under illustrative assumptions, six bespoke cases at six hours each require 36 hours; twelve hours of common preparation plus six deliveries at three hours each require 30. At two cases the shared arrangement requires 18 hours against 12. A ten-hour transition obligation makes the six-case shared arrangement require 40. These comparisons support only the stated work boundary; they still need timing, capability, funding and service conditions.

CUST.8 then asks what a changed “active” rule does to existing reports. Technical interface compatibility does not preserve an old report's meaning. The provider constructs a supported old profile, an agreed transition or another feasible continuation before changing that customer's provision.

Change one premise: the customer's data and worked examples may be used locally but not for a later customer or partner. Local success can remain valid. The common package needs a permitted alternative basis and requalification of any affected property. Its additional work belongs in CUST.7; technical portability supplies no permission.

### CUST.Reference:5.2 - Repeatable public learning provision

A public library offers digital-skills sessions. Another branch asks for translated materials, evening access, device help and a different route for residents who cannot attend in person.

The useful result is participation in a specified learning activity with the needed help, not merely distribution of a translated deck. CUST.2 distinguishes language, access, device preparation and facilitator capability. CUST.3 constructs a family around the common learning activity and its acceptance basis, with supported language and delivery variations. A need for continuing individual device repair falls outside the session offering and receives a separate service decision.

CUST.4 compares an assisted group session, a supported remote session and a local individualized arrangement. The choice includes the resident's actual preparation and access. CUST.5 uses permitted participation to learn whether the obstacle is the language, the device or missing help; it does not infer a general causal effect from one session.

CUST.6 prepares another facilitator through examples and practice, supplies device support and lets the receiving branch perform the session under the promised conditions. If one central expert is still needed for every difficult device, the method may be repeatable with that help, but expanding branches has not removed the central constraint.

CUST.7 compares the common preparation, facilitation, equipment, travel, coordination and continuing help against the programme's resource basis and public purpose. Donated time and residents' effort remain real contributions. A positive financial margin per participant is not an acceptance condition.

If a new remote platform replaces the old access route, CUST.8 constructs an attainable transition for current participants or preserves a bounded alternative. A more efficient provider workflow cannot by itself justify making the promised activity inaccessible to them.

## CUST.Reference:6 - Learn from Practice without Confusing the Result Levels

The field combines knowledge about customization and productization with practices that can correct that knowledge. Its recurring claims include the dependence of local results on their conditions; the relation between family invariants and variation; the work and support needed for repetition; the effect of volume, variety and time on burden; and the consequences of common changes for current obligations.

Those claims guide the eight Methods. Their application, in turn, can expose a false or too-broad claim. Compare explanations of the contrary case, qualify what the evidence supports and revise the general claim or the method's conditions when warranted. This is different from quietly adding a customer-specific exception while leaving the general claim untouched.

The characteristic of **CUST.1's result** is the coherence of repeatable customer commitments: the selected customer path, common contribution, delivery, resources and obligations fit together and can be reconstructed. The characteristic of **the discipline as a whole** is practice-constrained revisability of customization and productization knowledge: general claims and working Methods remain open to correction by qualified practice results. The first can hold for one case while the second fails.

For example, a provider funds author assistance, protects old obligations and successfully completes each customer case. Yet it keeps asserting that package P alone is sufficient for independent delivery in every environment S. Every instance of necessary author help is classified as a local exception and cannot change the general claim or the standard method. The customer paths may be coherent; the knowledge–practice relation is only one-way.

A different arrangement compares insufficient performer preparation, a package defect and an irreducible specialist contribution as explanations. It may qualify P as assisted provision in S, and independently usable only in a narrower S′ after adequate preparation. It changes the general statement and the corresponding delivery method while preserving supported customer work. That reciprocal correction is the field-level property.

A single successful case does not establish the property for a whole practice community. A missing observation leaves its state unknown. An unresolved question can remain part of the discipline while it has a meaningful route to investigation and revision. Replacing a claim or Method need not create a different field when the governed customer/common relation and reciprocal correction remain. Removing that relation, or treating field evidence as incapable of revising general knowledge, alters that field boundary rather than merely one method.

This field belongs within Management because its recurring decisions concern commitments, provision, resources and their reconsideration. Engineering, accounting and other external results contribute to those decisions without making their entire disciplines constituents of this one.

## CUST.Reference:7 - Recognition, Assurance and Correct Use

A symptom selects a useful question. Repeated expert rescue suggests a delivery-method problem; several similar requests suggest possible commonality; increased revenue suggests commercial activity. None of these observations alone establishes repeatability, a coherent family or lower marginal burden.

Obtain assurance for the claim actually used. A field attempt qualifies its tested conditions. A delivery trial can show what a prepared performer obtained with specified support. An economic comparison depends on its population, period, resource categories and assumptions. Technical compatibility and authority to change a promise remain different questions. Reuse adequate results where their conditions match.

At the scope of the connected practice, ask whether the customer can obtain the selected result; whether every common contribution has a supported form and receiving use; whether the needed decisions, capabilities and permissions are available together; whether continuing burden is included; and whether changed knowledge reaches the practices that rely on it. These questions inherit the relevant pattern-level answers.

The principal perspective risk is provider convenience. The payer's value can differ from the user's result, and a recipient can bear work that has disappeared from the provider's estimate. Include those participants when their work changes the answer. Accessible, cooperative customers can also bias field learning; qualify the population rather than claiming universality.

Several failures deserve specific correction. Payment can fund bespoke work but cannot make it repeatable. Moving work to a partner changes who performs it but may leave total burden and bottlenecks unchanged. An outcome metric can observe a result without giving the provider sufficient influence or evidence for its promise. A folder of reusable artifacts may lack the preparation and support through which another person obtains the result. The Methods address these different failures through different constructions.

## CUST.Reference:8 - Consequences

The framework can reduce private reconstruction by supplying both a large customer-case Method and directly usable smaller Methods. It makes local-only provision, assisted repetition, a narrower promise and refusal legitimate choices alongside common product development.

It also makes costs harder to hide. Common development, qualified transfer, support and migration can outweigh the benefit of repetition at a small volume or high variety. A constrained offering may be more supportable than a large configurable platform.

The additional work should be proportional to the live decision. A sufficient existing result ends that question. A low-risk configuration needs no full field study, and a retained local service needs no forced family admission.

## CUST.Reference:9 - Architectural Rationale

One framework serves the connected field because the local/shared decisions repeatedly constrain one another. Splitting customization from productization would put their joins back into each practitioner's private work. Placing all of the account inside Marketing, Systems Engineering or Operations would obscure the other receiving decisions; those frameworks supply Methods at their own scopes.

CUST.1 constructs a compatible continuation through decisions, intermediate results, joint conditions and returns. CUST.2 through CUST.8 retain independent working problems and reusable results. This allows convenient large use and flexible smaller use at the same time.

Known operations can form a useful new composite Method when their connection changes the first useful action or removes substantial private reconstruction. The supplying frameworks contribute results to this field; their disciplines are not all constituents of CUST.

A direct supplier is the better entry when its complete result answers the current question. Use SYSE.8 for an integrated offering/provider concept, IS.3 for constructing implementation support, or MA.8 for customer and product economics when no additional CUST join is missing. CUST explains when those results must be connected to local variation, a common family and continuing obligations.

A later treatment that provides this same connected use more clearly, or evidence that two independently useful fields need separate maintenance, can change the arrangement.

## CUST.Reference:10 - Sources and Synthesis

The source lines answer different questions. Service productization explains how an offering can become sufficiently specified and organized for repetition. Product-family and mass-customization work explains commonality, solution-space boundaries and customer choice. Order-decoupling and postponement work explains where common preparation ends and customer-dependent work begins. Field-engineering accounts explain continuing contact between local implementation and product development. Solution and outcome-based work connects provision, relationships, responsibility and economics.

CUST adopts those contributions at their stated reach. It rejects a universal “local success becomes product” sequence, a universal advantage of postponement, and an inference from a vendor's organizational description to measured effectiveness. Existing full framework Methods provide practical engineering, implementation, accounting and operating treatments; a limited external abstract is not used to replace them.

### CUST.Reference:10.1 - Productization, families and customer choice

- [Wirtz, Fritze, Jaakkola, Gelbrich and Hartley, “Service products and productization” (2021)](https://web2-bschool.nus.edu.sg/wp-content/uploads/media_rp/publications/sx3Ej1630635520.pdf), DOI 10.1016/j.jbusres.2021.08.033. The abstract, Sections 3–4 and selected discussion in Sections 5–6 support specification of a service product and its organized provision. This is a conceptual contribution, not measured evidence that CUST improves performance. CUST adapts the commercial framing for public and nonprofit provision while retaining actual resource requirements.
- [Valtakoski and Järvi, “Productization of knowledge-intensive services: Enabling knowledge sharing and cross-unit collaboration” (2016)](https://research.aalto.fi/fi/publications/productization-of-knowledge-intensive-services-enabling-knowledge/), DOI 10.1108/JOSM-01-2015-0004. The primary abstract of two longitudinal cases supports attention to goals, shared understanding and collaboration. CUST.6 draws on Implementation Facilitation for its transfer method.
- [Salvador, de Holan and Piller, “Cracking the Code of Mass Customization” (2009)](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265498057_Cracking_the_Code_of_Mass_Customization). The article's main text and three-capability account provide the historical anchor for solution-space development, robust process design and choice navigation, including services. CUST.3 and CUST.4 retain the three distinct questions instead of treating customization as a menu of features.
- [Simpson, Siddique and Jiao, “Platform-Based Product Family Development” (2006)](https://www.me.psu.edu/simpson/courses/me546/Platform.Chp01.w-Refs.pdf). The bounded chapter treatment, especially printed pages 4–6, supports top-down family development and bottom-up consolidation, with a commonality/differentiation tradeoff.
- [Bakås, Buer, Skjelstad and Kløve, “A Framework for Solution Space Development in Mass Customization” (2023)](https://www.sintef.no/en/publications/publication/2174785/), DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-34821-1_15. The primary abstract supports a continuing front-end/back-end learning account. Use CUST.3 and its supplying Methods to construct the family.

These contributions favor an explainable common basis and permitted variation over premature standardization. They leave room for useful local residue. When similarity is merely superficial, CUST keeps separate offerings rather than forcing one family.

### CUST.Reference:10.2 - Differentiation and its operating consequences

- [Olhager, “Strategic positioning of the order penetration point” (2003)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925527303001191), DOI 10.1016/S0925-5273(03)00119-1. The primary abstract and indexed introduction support the distinction between forecast-driven common work and order-driven work.
- [Harfeldt-Berg and Olhager, “The customer order decoupling point in empirical operations and supply chain management research: a systematic literature review” (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1080/00207543.2024.2314164). The primary indexed abstract establishes a broad empirical review and multiple contextual factors.
- [Naldi, Galizia and Bortolini, “Balancing storage cost and customization time in product platform design: a bi-objective optimization model” (2025)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00170-025-15081-1). Its model and stated assumptions make competing time and storage objectives concrete. Deterministic demand, cost and time, just-in-time custom components, sufficient warehouse space and the treatment of production cost bound the result. CUST.4 retains the tradeoff but does not transfer the model unchanged to software or services.

The serious alternative is early differentiation or entirely order-driven work. CUST.4 compares these with a shared base and later differentiation using the actual delay, resource and variation constraints.

### CUST.Reference:10.3 - Field work and return to the common offering

The official distinction between work on a capability for many customers and work across capabilities for one customer illustrates different directions of engineering attention. It is an organizational description, not independent causal evidence.
- [akshayk, “Who are Palantir FDEs?” (15 July 2026)](https://community.palantir.com/t/who-are-palantir-fdes/6847/4). The complete text, excluding linked images and video, is a practitioner's account of continuing field/product learning. It qualifies a reading of field work as only a temporary probe. Its experience claims remain those of the author.
- [OpenAI, Forward Deployed Engineer role description](https://openai.com/careers/forward-deployed-engineer-singapore-singapore/). The official role description connects implementation, adoption, reusable practices and feedback to product teams. It describes intended work rather than demonstrating an outcome.

CUST.5 retains the durable field/product connection while bounding each inquiry and protecting current service. A permanent function can perform many bounded inquiries; it need not remain one endless pilot. Negative evidence and a useful local-only outcome are valid receiving results.

### CUST.Reference:10.4 - Solutions, provision and outcome promises

- [Tuli, Kohli and Bharadwaj, “Rethinking Customer Solutions: From Product Bundles to Relational Processes” (2007)](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1509/jmkg.71.3.001). The primary abstract supports the relation between requirements, integration, deployment and subsequent support.
- [Storbacka, “A solution business model: Capabilities and management practices for integrated solutions” (2011)](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/251730722_A_solution_business_model_Capabilities_and_management_practices_for_integrated_solutions). The author-posted abstract supports attention to commercialization and industrialization across solution work.

The abstract and indexed publisher passages support continuing alignment of value creation and capture, rather than relying on contract form alone.
- [Rolls-Royce, TotalCare](https://www.rolls-royce.com/products-and-services/civil-aerospace/services/totalcare.aspx). The official offer illustrates selected engine-life and maintenance responsibilities and payment related to engine flying hours while the customer retains operational responsibilities. It is neither the actual contract nor independent evidence of performance.

CUST.4 uses the complete SYSE.8 offering/provider Method for the consequential choice. The provider's influence, other parties' contributions, observation, acceptance, risk and resources must support the promise. Observability alone is insufficient; complete control of every cause is not a universal prerequisite. A narrower supported promise remains an available result.

## CUST.Reference:12 - Use and Refresh

This document declares DocID CUST within FPF Library. Its CUST pattern addresses identify the individual contributions; CUST.Reference addresses this whole account, and CUST.Reminder addresses the optional working reminder. The framework is a constituent of the [Management DPF Suite](README.md), whose [Architectural Reference](MANAGEMENT-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md) explains wider connections.

The Readme selects three ordinary entries: CUST-ENTRY-DELIVERY, CUST-ENTRY-CHANGE and CUST-ENTRY-GROWTH. These are examples, not a taxonomy.

Use the complete current supplying treatment when a consequential condition has changed. Reopen the affected CUST contribution when a family invariant no longer holds, ordinary delivery needs different preparation or help, a permission changes, an operating constraint defeats a promise, or an old customer dependency alters the support tail. Preserve adequate unaffected contributions.

External source limits remain part of their use. An abstract can orient a question; obtain the full treatment when its procedure is needed. An official offer or job description can change or disappear; verify its current form before relying on that organizational fact. A relevant new result can change a particular construction, boundary or comparison.

## CUST.Reference:End

# Customization and Productization Management Patterns

## CUST.1 - Manage Client Variation and Develop Repeatable Offerings

> **Type:** Method pattern
> **Status:** Stable

### CUST.1:1 - Problem frame

Use this method when a customer difference affects both a particular result and the offering you expect to provide again. Typical signs are a successful workaround with an unclear support future, an integration sold before anyone has accepted its maintenance, or repeated services that still depend on their original author.

The first move is to place the actual supported offering beside the intended customer result and explain what must change. This exposes a choice richer than “standard product or bespoke project”: a common component, a repeatable assisted service and a local adaptation may belong in one feasible answer.

If the current offering already fits and can be provided under its ordinary conditions, use it. If only one bounded difficulty remains, enter the relevant smaller method. The full composition is useful when local and shared choices constrain one another.

### CUST.1:2 - Problem

Local urgency tends to make the next delivery decisive. Shared development tends to treat local work as a source of product requests. Neither view alone settles who may promise what, which work is funded, whether another performer can repeat it or what happens to existing customers. The missing result is a jointly supportable continuation.

### CUST.1:3 - Forces

| Tension | Decision it changes |
| --- | --- |
| Immediate value and future repetition | Whether to deliver locally now, invest in a common contribution or retain the present offering. |
| One customer contact and distinct decision rights | Who can speak for the whole promise without silently deciding architecture, spending and assurance. |
| Commonality and useful difference | Which variations preserve the result and which need a separate offering. |
| Learning and current service | How to obtain an answer without consuming resources already promised elsewhere. |
| Wider use and continuing obligations | Whether the proposed shared release can coexist with installed configurations and support commitments. |

### CUST.1:4 - Solution

#### CUST.1:4.1 - Recover the two receiving results

Describe what the customer needs to be able to do, with whom, under which conditions and by when. Identify the evidence of an adequate result and the parties whose acceptance matters. Then recover the provider's present offering: supported inputs, configurations, delivery work, assistance, exclusions and continuing obligations. Use the actual agreement and operating practice, not only the sales description.

Ask separately what the present case needs and what a later customer or performer might receive. The second result might be a reusable component, an extension, a delivery method, a training contribution or no common change. Treat it as a candidate until its scope and provision are supported. A local success does not select its shared form.

Keep any sufficient result already available. An earlier qualified configuration can settle a technical choice while leaving a new response-time promise unresolved. Carry that remaining difference into the work; do not reopen the settled configuration merely to make every case follow the same sequence.

#### CUST.1:4.2 - Turn the differences into compatible alternatives

Work backward from the missing customer result, then forward through the proposed delivery. Compare inputs, meanings, operations, decisions, access, help, acceptance and support with the supported basis. The constructive method in [CUST.2](#cust2---recover-client-deltas-and-choose-their-disposition) explains this recovery. Its result must tell the receiving decision what differs and why it matters.

Develop at least the materially different feasible continuations. These can include the supported offering unchanged, an allowed configuration, a bounded local adaptation, a shared component or family extension, a repeatable service, a partner contribution, a narrower promise and refusal. Combine them when their conditions fit. A partner can perform a repeatable service built around a common component while one report remains local.

For each serious alternative, trace the customer's complete result. A technical adapter is incomplete if nobody can operate it. A paid exception is incomplete if the fee does not obtain the needed specialist. An outcome promise is incomplete if the provider arrangement and evidence cannot support its stated responsibility. Use the corresponding full professional method to obtain that missing result, then bring its conditions back into the alternative.

#### CUST.1:4.3 - Make the consequential decisions governable

Before an irreversible promise, identify who can contribute and decide the following matters in this case. These are decision-bearing contributions, not a mandatory headcount or organization chart.

| Contribution | What must be made available | Boundary that must not be decided silently elsewhere |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer result and acceptance | The useful result, relevant participants and an intelligible acceptance basis. | A provider's convenient demonstration must not replace the customer's required result. |
| Local realization | A feasible way to obtain that result in the customer's actual setting. | A local workaround must not become a promise of general availability or permanent support. |
| Common offering and family | A reasoned decision to admit, limit, defer or reject a common contribution. | One sale must not determine the supported family without its consequences. |
| Repeatable delivery and support | A method, preparation and assistance that another qualified performer can obtain. | A manual or handover must not conceal continuing dependence on its author. |
| Resources and economics | The work, capacity, funding and continuing burden of each alternative. | Commercial enthusiasm must not waive an unavailable resource or conceal unfunded work. |
| Evidence and permitted use | The grounds, permissions and assurance needed for the consequential claim or action. | Delivery success must not certify its own broad repeatability, safety or reuse rights. |

Name the person or group with actual authority for each live decision, the inputs they need, the next decision time and the conditions they may not waive alone. The person making the customer promise needs the joined answer, even when another party supplied each contribution.

One competent person may supply several contributions. Keep the distinctions visible in the decision itself: “I can implement this locally; I have not committed the product team to support it.” Seek independent judgement when incentives, uncertainty or consequences make self-approval unreliable, or when applicable professional conditions require it. The independence may concern one consequential evidence claim rather than every small change. Reconsider bundled responsibilities when workload, value at risk or disagreement makes the arrangement ineffective.

When actual positions, assignments or enabling relations must change, use [OCE.5 — Define Organization Positions](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce5---define-organization-positions) and [OCE.6 — Establish Holder Assignments and Enabling Relations for Organization Change](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce6---establish-holder-assignments-and-enabling-relations-for-organization-change). Receive an arrangement with real decision rights, capability, time and access, then use it here. If a required authority or resource is absent, narrow or defer the dependent promise while preserving independent permitted work.

#### CUST.1:4.4 - Obtain the missing contribution without losing the whole

Choose the next action by the uncertainty that can change the alternative. A known local modification needs implementation, not a research programme. A disputed meaning needs semantic work. Uncertain transfer may need a field inquiry. A capacity conflict needs an operating answer.

For customer inquiry, [MKT.12 — Investigate a Customer or Market Question for a Decision](MARKETING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mkt12---investigate-a-customer-or-market-question-for-a-decision) supplies the question, discriminating evidence and permitted information use. For implementation difficulty, [IS.1 — Agree a Useful Implementation-Support Undertaking](../IMPLEMENTATION-FACILITATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#is1---agree-a-useful-implementation-support-undertaking) and [IS.2 — Find the Implementation Difficulty and Obtain the Next Useful Contribution](../IMPLEMENTATION-FACILITATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#is2---find-the-implementation-difficulty-and-obtain-the-next-useful-contribution) establish the undertaking and the next useful contribution; [IS.3 — Construct and Adapt a Support Strategy with Its Recipients](../IMPLEMENTATION-FACILITATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#is3---construct-and-adapt-a-support-strategy-with-its-recipients) constructs support with its recipients. Receive their bounded result, not just a completed activity. For example, “the team has attended training” does not yet settle whether the deployment is obtainable.

Use [CUST.5](#cust5---run-field-learning-and-return-a-productization-candidate) when field work must answer both the local question and a shared-development question. Preserve stopped, inconclusive and local-only outcomes. Protect current service while the question is open. If a result changes the interpretation of the customer's need or the supported basis, return to those affected choices before continuing.

#### CUST.1:4.5 - Construct the common continuation and its delivery

When sharing could help, build the family through [CUST.3](#cust3---develop-a-repeatable-offering-family): common result and conditions, invariants, allowed variations, forbidden combinations and the local residue. The same artifact can belong in one family and be unusable in another because support, permission or customer work differs.

Make a customer choice through [CUST.4](#cust4---configure-a-customer-solution-and-place-differentiation). Join that choice to the actual delivery method through [CUST.6](#cust6---establish-repeatable-deployment-and-service-delivery). The explanation, tools, preparation and support must enable another prepared performer to obtain the intended result. Assistance can remain part of that method.

A technical platform decision remains with its engineering method. Obtain the architecture, interface or supported-use result and use it to define the family and delivery conditions. If it supports only a narrower class, narrow the offering rather than treating technical approval as permission for every customer promise.

#### CUST.1:4.6 - Join economics, responsibility and present customers

Compare the complete alternatives on the same result, period and customer set. [CUST.7](#cust7---evaluate-growth-and-customization-with-full-resource-obligations) includes common preparation, local execution, qualification, specialist help, support, migration and retirement. Distinguish an investment from an ordinary delivery charge and from an existing obligation. Confirm that funding and capacity exist when needed.

For a changed engineering offering or outcome arrangement, obtain the complete concept through [SYSE.8 — Develop an Integrated Offering and Provider Concept for Using an Engineered Result](../Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse8---develop-an-integrated-offering-and-provider-concept-for-using-an-engineered-result). Bring back the participating systems and parties, contributions, responsibility, operating conditions, observation and acceptance, and the risks retained by each party. Use that result to revise the family, resource comparison and customer agreement. Obtain the relevant professional method and evidence when the promised result extends beyond engineering.

Use [CUST.8](#cust8---change-the-offering-family-with-compatible-customer-transitions) before a common change affects existing customers. Reconcile their configurations, results, support and promises with the proposed release. A technically compatible interface can still change an agreed operating burden.

The joint decision must hold together: the customer can obtain the result; the selected local and common forms are permitted and supported; the required work fits actual means; existing obligations have a feasible continuation. Failure of one condition reopens the dependent choice. It does not erase every useful result already obtained.

#### CUST.1:4.7 - Close a bounded result and retain its return

Finish with an executable local continuation and a distinct shared-development disposition. Examples are “deliver the existing configuration,” “provide the local service with funded specialist help; investigate a common adapter separately,” or “decline the unsupported outcome promise while offering a bounded contribution.”

Leave the receiving participants able to recognize what was decided, what remains uncertain, who supplies the next contribution and what change reopens the decision. A short agreed explanation can suffice.

Return recurring practice results to the general knowledge they test. If every transferred deployment needs its author, distinguish a defect in this family from a wider mistaken claim about what makes delivery repeatable. Revise that claim only on appropriate grounds; local exceptions must not indefinitely protect an unsupported general rule.

### CUST.1:5 - Archetypal Grounding

A provider offers an analytical service from a standard batch file. A new customer requests private hosting, SSO, a different meaning of “active account,” a local report and urgent support. The service lead begins with the customer's decision use: a monthly eligibility decision, not merely a dashboard installation.

CUST.2 separates the five differences and their dependencies. The identity provider already fits a supported interface. “Active” requires a semantic answer before the computation can be accepted. Private hosting needs a bounded field attempt. The report can remain a local service. Urgent support competes for an existing specialist.

The lead and field engineer are the same person, but that person cannot commit the product maintainer's future support. The customer accepts the eligibility meaning; the engineer proposes the deployment; the product maintainer decides the common interface; the delivery lead supplies a repeatable run; the capacity holder commits support; an appropriate independent specialist checks the consequential security claim. Several contributions can be supplied by the same people, but no disagreement is silently converted into a promise.

A successful private-hosting attempt yields a family candidate with two supported environments and an explicit exclusion for disconnected operation. The delivery team receives a rehearsed setup method with scheduled specialist assistance. The report remains local. A wider rollout waits because the support resource cannot yet cover both existing customers and the new response time.

Change the condition: materials obtained for the first customer cannot be shared with a partner. Local provision may continue. The family and delivery work must obtain permitted alternative material or stop that transfer.

In a public library service, the same composition can connect local language and accessibility needs with reusable teaching materials and supported facilitators. Funding and workload replace customer margin as the relevant resource questions. Educational effectiveness still requires educational grounds.

### CUST.1:6 - Bias-Annotation

The method makes coordination visible and can encourage over-organization. Use the smallest actual arrangement capable of the decisions. A small team can retain one customer contact and combine compatible contributions. Cases with infrequent customization may be better served by a known local method than a maintained family.

The examples emphasize observable delivery. Less tangible service results require appropriate subject expertise rather than a convenient proxy such as document completion.

### CUST.1:7 - Conformance Checklist

- Can the participants distinguish the customer's result from the proposed common result?
- Are consequential differences recovered from real work, including assistance and continuing support?
- Do the people making promises have the required contributions and authority?
- Does the selected combination have compatible conditions, resources and evidence?
- Are local-only, unchanged, stopped and inconclusive outcomes allowed?
- Can existing customers continue under supported obligations?
- Can the next recipient act without reconstructing the missing joins privately?

### CUST.1:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

**One person decides everything implicitly.** Keep the live decisions distinct and obtain a qualified counterview where the consequence warrants it.

**A route replaces construction.** “Send to product” says who might receive a question, not what family should be built. Develop the result and its receiving conditions.

**The customer paid, so the exception scales.** Payment can fund work. Determine whether the scarce work actually changes at the intended volume.

**Every case must become common.** Preserve a useful bounded local result when its transfer is unsupported or uneconomic.

### CUST.1:9 - Consequences

The method can make local service and shared development mutually intelligible, with less hidden commitment. It also exposes work that was previously unpaid or unowned. That may produce a smaller promise, additional investment or refusal rather than a larger common product.

Its additional coordination is worthwhile only where the connected decisions matter. Sufficient smaller methods remain available directly.

### CUST.1:10 - Architectural Rationale

The whole method is organized around two receiving results and their shared constraints. Its smaller methods can be used independently, but their availability does not itself provide the joining decisions for a customer case.

A fixed sequence would reopen settled questions and delay urgent responses. Pure local discretion would hide common obligations. The conditional composition retains enough structure to coordinate both while allowing justified short paths.

### CUST.1:11 - SoTA-Echoing

The useful source line combines service productization, bounded solution spaces and continuing field/product learning. Compared with “standardize everything” or “let field teams solve each case,” it preserves explicit variation, assistance and a path back to common development.

Wirtz and colleagues' conceptual account of service productization supports defining and systematizing an offering; Salvador, de Holan and Piller's mass-customization account adds solution-space development, robust processes and choice navigation. CUST adapts those contributions and combines them with the full Management, Engineering and Implementation Facilitation methods named above.

Official FDE role descriptions and the practitioner account discussed in CUST.Reference:10 support continuing interaction between local delivery and product development. They do not establish that one staffing model causes better results. Reconsider the composition when another available treatment provides the same connected use more adequately or when its own coordination cost exceeds the benefit.

### CUST.1:12 - Relations

CUST.2 through CUST.8 supply conditional constituent methods of CUST.1. Their outputs are joined by the customer result, permission, resource and continuing-obligation conditions in this Solution. Their publication order is not a work schedule.

[MKT.11 — Align Promises, Partners and Execution](MARKETING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mkt11---align-promises-partners-and-execution) supplies promise/execution alignment; [MKT.13 — Test Commercial Model Repeatability and Deployment Limits](MARKETING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mkt13---test-commercial-model-repeatability-and-deployment-limits) supplies commercial repeatability and deployment-limit inquiry; [MKT.14 — Develop and Change a Programme for Selected Customer Organisations](MARKETING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mkt14---develop-and-change-a-programme-for-selected-customer-organisations) supplies the customer-organization programme. Use their complete methods when those questions arise and return their qualified results to the selected alternative.

CUST.Reference:2 explains the field boundary; CUST.Reference:3 distinguishes composition, supplied results and a repertoire.

### CUST.1:End

## CUST.2 - Recover Client Deltas and Choose Their Disposition

> **Type:** Method pattern
> **Status:** Stable

### CUST.2:1 - Problem frame

Use this method when “the customer needs customization” conceals several different changes, or when a completed deployment contains unexplained local work. You need a supported basis, an intended or observed customer result, and access to the people or material that can reveal the consequential work.
