Follow what people actually do and what the receiver obtains. Notice who takes initiative, whose concern gets a response, which commitments hold and which support was decisive. Ask participants about consequential differences between the proposed and experienced work. Inspect non-participation before choosing its explanation: a missing time window, a mistaken promise and rejection of the aim call for different responses.

Reconsider the part whose premise changed. Failed integration can require a better subject method. An accepted workload that no longer fits needs a changed agreement. A useful result for the wrong population can require a revised direction and different participants. If the first experience changes what people consider worth doing, return to that purpose instead of treating their earlier acceptance as permanent consent.

Continue with adequate arrangements and support. Distribute further leadership only where people can and wish to take the contribution and the work permits it. LDR.1 develops or obtains the needed capability; HCD supplies human learning, and CB supplies continuing community participation when that becomes the actual undertaking. End an exhausted or unsupported collaboration while settling its existing commitments through their applicable arrangements.

Return both the useful work and the justified account: what people could undertake together, which conditions made it possible, and what remains unsettled. Evidence of a bounded collaboration supports its warranted continuation. C.28 is needed for a causal-effect claim, and C.36 for a cultural-continuation claim.

### LDR.5:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### LDR.5:5.1 - A direction before a software project's next release plan

Suppose an open-source project's maintainer proposes a major rewrite after several late releases. Contributors agree that the delays are frustrating, but nobody has agreed to the rewrite. The maintainer controls acceptance into the maintained repository under its existing rules; contributors control their voluntary time, and users decide whether they can adopt a release.

A contributor offers to convene a short inquiry. A documentation author, an integration specialist and two users accept the exchange. One user cannot disclose an installation's data but can describe the required compatibility. The group needs that boundary condition, not the protected data. Their accounts reveal different concerns: the maintainer wants less support work, a contributor wants to try a new design, and users need a stable version. The specialist shows a repeated gap between accepting contributions and having someone available to integrate them.

The proposed explanation changes. The domain comparison finds that an isolated adapter can remove the immediate integration difficulty without a rewrite; the new design remains a possible later undertaking. For this stipulated case, the participants consider maintaining the current release with that adapter, undertaking the rewrite and retiring active support. They choose a bounded maintenance direction because it meets the current users' need at a contribution the volunteers can actually supply. The design enthusiast declines maintenance and continues independent exploration without committing the project's name or release promise.

The integration specialist offers to lead one adapter attempt. The maintainer accepts that technical initiative while retaining release acceptance. The author offers an installation explanation; the users offer permitted compatibility observations. Each can explain why an incompatible new feature will wait. LDR.2 resolves their date and support terms, and LDR.4 supplies any remaining first-use preparation. A capable ordinary exchange can already provide those results.

In the constructed first use, the adapter supports the intended installation. The group has a useful maintenance result and evidence about this collaboration. It has neither a consensus on the rewrite nor an obligation from the participant who declined. The working account now connects an actual user purpose, technical grounds, accepted initiative and feasible contributions. That is more than the original agreement that delays were frustrating.

#### LDR.5:5.2 - Change the consequence, not merely the project name

Now suppose the compatibility inquiry shows that the adapter cannot support the intended installation. The maintenance direction has lost a technical premise. The maintainer returns the finding and its limits; the group reconsiders retirement, a narrower supported installation or a differently resourced rewrite. The previously declined contribution remains declined. A stronger appeal to loyalty supplies no missing technical way.

Change a different condition instead: the adapter remains adequate, but the integration specialist loses the offered time. Keep the technical result and reconsider the contribution through LDR.2 and LDR.1. There is no reason to reopen everybody's purposes unless the changed burden alters the direction they can support.

#### LDR.5:5.3 - A manager's decision with limited room for participation

Suppose a service manager must reduce evening coverage under an already authorized budget decision. The decision about expenditure is outside the team's present remit; the allocation of remaining coverage and the treatment of unanswered requests are open. Pretending that the whole decision awaits consensus would mislead staff.

The manager states those boundaries and obtains accounts from the affected shifts and service recipients. Their concerns show that a proposed uniform reduction leaves one promised receiving window uncovered. The domain and operations work supplies feasible alternatives; the manager obtains the required decisions on the affected promise. Staff can influence the workable arrangement, raise unresolved concerns and understand their actual assignments without being asked to endorse the budget rationale. A staff member's personal development aim enters a role conversation where it changes the allocation.

If the purpose, allocation, authority and receiving conditions were already adequate, perform the ordinary brief and the work. This method would add no useful direction-setting result. Conversely, if the budget decision's premise is defeated by new evidence, return that evidence to the body able to reconsider it; neither the manager nor the team acquires a new power merely by agreeing.

### LDR.5:6 - Bias-Annotation

The method favours participants having a real part in forming what they will do. An initiator can simulate this while keeping every consequential choice closed. An articulate participant can also dominate the account. Use actual decision boundaries, the experience needed for the question and feasible ways for less visible contributors to be heard. Protected work and legitimate urgent authority can limit participation; disclose the resulting limit instead of claiming a fully shared decision.

### LDR.5:7 - Conformance Checklist

- The connection among participants is established from the situation and its consequences; the roster and common purpose are not merely presumed.
- Observations, interpretations, desired results and remedies can be distinguished and corrected.
- The direction has a substantive basis and a meaningful alternative; agreement does not supply its professional warrant.
- Participants can relate the direction to their own purposes, contributions and limits, with formal duties distinguished from voluntary commitments.
- The first action has the contributions and authority it needs, and participants can explain a consequential choice under its terms.
- Later responses revise the affected purpose, arrangement or method while preserving valid results and commitments.

### LDR.5:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Invited mistake | Better action |
| --- | --- |
| Treat a shared complaint as agreement to the founder's solution. | Reconstruct the experience and compare the direction with the people whose action it requires. |
| Announce consultation after every consequential decision has been made. | State the actual open questions and the binding decisions; let relevant input change the former. |
| Explain non-participation through a personality or motivation label. | Inspect the actual contribution, participant's account and conditions before choosing a response. |
| Make an accepted direction permanent consent to later sacrifices. | Return a consequential change in burden or purpose to the affected participants and decision holders. |
| Require consensus before every valid ordinary action. | Retain adequate agreement and authority, and use the sufficient working conversation. |

### LDR.5:9 - Consequences

Participants can develop a direction and take initiative without first receiving a finished plan from a designated leader. The group can discover that its initial proposal addressed the wrong problem or that only a narrower collaboration is warranted. Obtaining and responding to people's experience costs time and can expose conflicts that the initiator cannot resolve. A sound result may be separate action or refusal.

### LDR.5:10 - Rationale

Joint direction is produced through the relation between an interpreted situation, worthwhile possibilities and people's actual ability and willingness to act. Changing any one can change the others. Constructing these relations before demanding commitment explains why the method can begin without a ready proposal, yet still needs the separate subject, agreement and authority results before action. A later experience returns to the premise it changes, rather than restarting the whole relationship or demanding renewed enthusiasm.

### LDR.5:11 - SoTA-Echoing

**Adapt** [Ganz's 2010 treatment of leadership in social movements](https://dash.harvard.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/7312037d-c5ad-6bd4-e053-0100007fdf3b/content) as a developed historical comparison: relationships, purposes, strategic reasoning and actual commitments must connect, especially where participation is voluntary. The present method retains those questions while supplying its own bounded construction. It does not transfer movement-specific narrative forms or presume that a founder represents an affected population.

**Use narrowly** [DeRue and Ashford's 2010 theoretical proposal](https://doi.org/10.5465/amr.35.4.zok627) that leadership identity is constructed through claims and grants in interaction. The claim-and-grant distinction directs attention to the other participants' responses; it does not establish that a title or a successful appeal obtains their recognition.

R10's leadership discussion supplies the person–role–work tension and mutual support for joint responsibility. The CCL comparison in LDR.Reference:1.3 supplies a collective-outcome view. These perspectives answer different questions. The construction also retains formal authority, legitimate refusal and independent professional judgement, which the actual setting may require together.

The serious alternatives are a competent direct conversation, an already sufficient strategic process with actual participation, CB.1 for a community contribution, and LDR.2 or LDR.4 for a sufficiently formed proposal. Retain them where they supply the needed result. This method earns its additional work when participants must still construct what they can undertake together and how initiative will be exercised. Its use depends on the stated participation, knowledge and authority conditions. Reopen the method when a simpler available approach supplies that result, an important group or consequence was omitted, or experience defeats its explanation.

### LDR.5:12 - Relations

LDR.1 supplies capable help and the role conversation. LDR.2 constructs compatible accepted contributions; LDR.4 carries an examinable proposal through effective decision and first use. Enter either directly when the prior result is already available.

[Strategy (STR)](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md), STR.5/.6/.18, supplies the worthwhile contribution, obtaining way and coherent strategic judgement. [Community Management (CB)](COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md), CB.1 and CB.13, supplies a useful community contribution and a workable shared-decision mandate. These results can participate in leadership work without becoming substitutes for actual participation.

FPF B.5.SD supplies subject reasoning through discussion; D.4 supplies value-conflict reasoning; C.11.DUA appraises further inquiry. OCE.2/.10 supplies investigation where the subject is organizational work or participation. PSDA.12/.13 supplies professional participation and facilitation. Their wider methods retain their own conditions and results.

### LDR.5:End

# Connected use: a federation begins a joint evidence service

## LDR.Use:1 - A worthwhile proposal with incompatible contributions

The following is a constructed use of LDR.1, LDR.2, LDR.4 and the supplied answer construction. Its joint purpose and initial participation are already established; LDR.5 addresses the different starting condition in which they still need construction. It does not describe an observed organization or claim that these numbers apply elsewhere.

Suppose three independent engineering communities want a monthly service in which practitioners bring a difficult evidence package, obtain a qualified diagnosis and leave with an actionable correction. The wider purpose is to help members develop their practice. The present leadership question is narrower: can the communities begin and continue a supported first service?

A competent domain team has already designed the proposed diagnostic method and its acceptance conditions. Each case needs two hours of substantive integration and half an hour of a separate qualified acceptance decision. The case owner also needs to supply permitted material, attend the receiving conversation and perform any corrective engineering work. Those activities are part of the service arrangement; the two-and-a-half-hour figure does not include them.

Four cases are proposed for the first month. The available joint specialist capacity is eight hours, of which two must remain for previously accepted work. Six hours remain for the new service. In this case, the pool's members are qualified for both integration and acceptance, and compatible windows permit a different specialist to accept each case from the one who integrated it. The available hours can therefore be allocated between those activities without losing the required independence. Four cases would require ten hours of the constrained specialist work, so the proposal is infeasible before considering the clients' correction work. Enthusiasm does not change that result.

The organizer uses LDR.1 to identify the missing contributions: a domain integration provider, qualified acceptance, client preparation, participant communication and a decision about scarce time. These are functions in the work, not five new jobs. Existing community coordinators can communicate the agreed terms; no common office is needed for that contribution.

## LDR.Use:2 - Advice changes the promise

Using LDR.4, the organizer asks community representatives whose judgement they need before accepting the offer. One wants advice from a practitioner who helped with an earlier clinic. A permitted anonymized example lets that adviser expose a misleading promise: the service can diagnose the missing ground but cannot promise to complete an unknown amount of corrective engineering within the session.

The domain team and intended clients trace one representative case. They distinguish the service's diagnosis and bounded acceptance decision from the client's later correction work. Through B.5.SD they construct a clearer account: the receiver will get the warranted finding, its grounds, a feasible next question or correction, and the limitation on further reliance. A case with no attainable correction may properly end in deferral.

The revised promise changes both expectations and resources. The client must accept responsibility for obtaining corrective work, or the provider must quote and supply it separately. The communities do not solve this by improving the advertising language alone; they revise the offered work and the terms clients can accept.

## LDR.Use:3 - Agree a feasible first month

Using LDR.2, the participants compare several whole arrangements. Two cases need five of the six available specialist hours, leaving one hour for a stated exception reserve. Four cases with unchanged scope need ten hours and do not fit. Another qualified provider can supply the missing integration, but its fee exceeds the first month's available budget. Postponing every case loses the value of beginning, while splitting the same case among several partial reviewers adds handovers without removing its needed integration.

The communities choose two cases for the first month. The acceptance provider reserves one hour; the integration provider reserves four. The remaining hour is not promised twice. Clients supply permitted materials before the allocated window and reserve their receiving time. If an exception consumes more than the reserve, the affected correction or next case is reconsidered; the reserve is not a promise to finish arbitrary extra work.

Each representative can commit only their community's contribution under its actual rules. Individual clients accept their own terms. A host reserves the permitted communication service and maintains the agreed access; it does not thereby acquire authority over all communities. The same complete proposal, including the two-case limit and client correction boundary, receives the needed responses.

The organizer's preparation, consultation and scheduling time is separately supplied by the communities. It is not hidden inside the six specialist hours. If that contribution is unavailable, an already capable coordinator can be retained, a smaller preparation arranged, or the start deferred.

## LDR.Use:4 - Begin and complete a useful contribution

The organizer uses LDR.4 to obtain the effective permissions and make the start mutually visible. The providers and clients confirm the same scope, dates, input conditions and route for an unsupported claim. A shared message with actual confirmations suffices; the federation does not create a launch ceremony.

The first case reveals that a test concerns an earlier configuration. The integrator explains the changed condition and the unsupported conclusion. The acceptance provider judges the diagnostic result within its remit. The client now knows which release claim cannot be made and which engineering question must be answered. That is the promised bounded service result, not a corrected engineering package or evidence that the client has acquired independent mastery.

If the client expected a completed correction, the receiving result would fail the promise. The provider would need a revised service, resources and agreement rather than a new definition of success after the event.

The participants use LDR.1 to arrange continuation. The second case has the same qualified support; another coordinator can conduct the preparatory exchange without the initiator. Where human skill development is separately wanted, HCD supplies its design and assessment. Successful diagnosis alone does not establish that development.

## LDR.Use:5 - Qualified autonomous AI changes the feasible whole

Now change the performer condition. Suppose, for this scenario, a qualified autonomous AI service can perform the substantive integration under the same required acceptance conditions. Its qualification, permitted data handling, operating controls and availability are established for these cases. It can reserve routine service slots and return the diagnosis within an effective delegated mandate. It cannot make a decision reserved to the independent acceptance provider.

The setup requires four hours of one-time qualified configuration and onboarding before the month begins. That work has a separately available window and an accepted cost. Recurring human exception support requires one hour per month plus fifteen minutes per case. The independent acceptance still needs half an hour per case. Four cases therefore require one plus one plus two, or four hours of the constrained human capacity. They fit the six hours available; the agent's compute and service fee also require an accepted budget. For the same four-case result, the human arrangement needs ten hours of integration and acceptance plus the same one-hour exception reserve: eleven hours. The new arrangement needs four recurring hours, with its one-time setup stated separately. Client preparation, correction work and ordinary coordination remain necessary in both arrangements and are supplied outside this specialist allocation.

This can justify four cases without an additional office. The AI performs the integration and permitted scheduling; people do not repeat those operations merely to preserve former roles. The communities retain their real acceptance of the service terms, input permissions, client work and the independent decision the scenario still requires.

Change the authority and assurance condition again. Suppose a competent independent automated acceptance service is available, is permitted by the applicable rule, and supplies the required independent judgement without the earlier human half-hour per case. That contribution can also move to AI. The recurring human demand becomes the one-hour support provision plus the four fifteen-minute exception allocations: two hours. Independence is a property of the actual judging arrangement and grounds, not merely a second agent label. The responsible parties can now reconsider the larger service scope or retain the spare capacity; no automatic expansion follows.

In the opposite variation, the agent is qualified only to draft a summary and every case still requires the original two hours of expert integration. The promised reduction is unsupported. Four cases would still exceed the six hours, with the agent's cost added. Retain the two-case arrangement or obtain another feasible source of competence.

These are conditional comparisons, not claims about a named AI product. C.11.DUA keeps setup, recurring work, required guarantees, delay, fees and displaced work in view. Stronger competence changes architecture only where the real arrangement supports relying on it.

## LDR.Use:6 - Continuation after success is another substantive question

Suppose the first month's cases succeed under their stated conditions. The communities have evidence of a bounded service, not proof of a culture of continuing development. They also notice a weak signal: practitioners can correct known evidence gaps but rarely question whether their chosen problem is still worthwhile.

A participant raises that concern through LDR.1; B.5.SD can help formulate and examine it with the relevant development practitioners. The next development question is whether and how to build problem-discovery and problem-formulation capability, not simply how to schedule more clinics. The development method supplies the problem, attainable challenge and transition; strategy and portfolio methods reconcile its value and resources with other work.

Leadership then helps obtain the contributions for whichever next move is warranted. The useful first service continues if worth its cost. It can also be narrowed or discontinued. Keeping an offer alive and continuing the subject's development are related decisions with different results.

## LDR.Source:2 - Source contributions and evidence limits

The pattern comparisons state the claims that change the methods. The following notes make their boundaries recoverable without turning the sources into a generic reading requirement.

- **Organization Change Engineering, historical version of 3 October 2026, OCE.12**, supplies the source treatment of adequate ordinary coordination, human-development cost, negotiated whole proposals, substantive integration, proposal preparation and first-use cases.
- **R10, Systems Management**, in «Рабочие продукты и корпоративные ритуалы как видимая форма оргизменений» (work products and corporate rituals as visible forms of organizational change) and the preparation and decision passages of «Шаг развития: постановка оргвозможности» (a development step: establishing an organizational capability), supplies working products, trusted advice, proposal preparation and shared start. The present source use is bounded to those connected portions and the already developed OCE account; it is not a review of the whole Guide. The method is taught in LDR.4, so the reader need not reconstruct it from R10. Fixed durations, categorical claims about resistance and claims that all concerns are harmless are not adopted.
- **CCL, “What Is Leadership?”, 15 March 2026** supplies a relational conceptual comparison. It does not establish a complete leadership ontology or a measured effect of these leadership Methods and the supplied answer construction.
- **CBI, Mutual Gains Approach brief, 2023** supplies the negotiation comparison used in LDR.2. Its short source account is supplemented by the developed joint-feasibility and receiving-use construction here.
- **IAF Core Competencies, revised 6 December 2021** supplies the competent-facilitation alternative for B.5.SD. A professional competency account is not a domain-specific calculation or an effectiveness study.
- **AHRQ TeamSTEPPS 3.0 brief, huddle and debrief pages**, reviewed in 2023, supply concrete teamwork comparators for LDR.1 and LDR.4. No healthcare outcome estimate or permission is transferred to the constructed non-clinical cases.
- **CFIR Opinion Leaders**, current guide, supplies the informal-judgement cue and its limits in LDR.4. Identifying influence does not supply the actual advice, representation or agreement.
- **“Об фасилитаторов,” 25 May 2020**, supplies a diagnostic practitioner criticism used in B.5.SD. Broad empirical claims and categorical conclusions about facilitators are not premises of the method.

Sources linked in a predecessor's bibliography but not used for a claim here do not silently become evidence for this publication. The conditional cases and arithmetic support the illustrated choices under their stipulated premises. They are not practitioner trials, demonstrations of universal transfer or causal evaluations.

The field explanation also uses the following bounded source comparisons:

- **R10, chapter “Практика лидерства”,** especially “Лидерство как практика изготовления организаций”, “Лидерство для достижения уровней сотрудничества” and “Личное целеполагание как практика лидерства”, connects the person's agency, performed roles, organizational conditions, mutual support and goal conversations. This publication develops those connections beyond a ready organization design. It does not adopt universal claims that good cooperation requires an already good design, that everyone must lead, that goals are exclusively individual, or that a particular goal-setting practice is always best.
- **[CCL, Direction + Alignment + Commitment, 15 March 2026](https://www.ccl.org/articles/leading-effectively-articles/make-leadership-happen-with-dac-framework/)** supplies the collective-outcome comparison in Reference:1.3. Its model is a useful view, not a universal classification or evidence of this publication's effect.
- **[Ganz, Leading Change, 2010](https://dash.harvard.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/7312037d-c5ad-6bd4-e053-0100007fdf3b/content),** the introduction and relationship account, supplies a historical developed treatment of shared purpose and voluntary participation before a settled hierarchy. LDR.5 states the adapted contribution and the boundary of its use.
- **[Manz, 1986](https://doi.org/10.5465/AMR.1986.4306232), abstract,** supplies the historical distinction between self-influence and merely meeting externally supplied standards. Reference:1.6 connects the personal-development question to the complete Strategy and HCD methods; the abstract supplies no procedural or effectiveness evidence.
- **[DeRue and Ashford, 2010](https://doi.org/10.5465/amr.35.4.zok627), abstract,** supplies only the claim-and-grant distinction. The abstract is not treated as a complete method or an empirical result.
- **[Edmondson, 1999](https://web.mit.edu/curhan/www/docs/Articles/15341_Readings/Organizational_Learning_and_Change/Edmondson_1999_Psychological_safety.pdf),** the construct, discussion and limitations, supplies a historical empirical comparison concerning speaking, learning and structural support. The single-company cross-sectional design limits causal and cross-setting inference; this text transfers no measured effect.
- **[Google re:Work, Set goals with OKRs](https://rework.withgoogle.com/intl/en/guides/set-goals-with-okrs), originally 2016,** supplies the counterexample to treating OKRs as exclusively personal goals and the distinction from employee evaluation. Its company practice is an available option rather than the field's mandatory current method.

These theories, empirical observations and practitioner accounts have different roles. The source comparisons inform the construction and expose alternatives; the conditional cases examine this publication's reasoning. Neither source age nor a current web page establishes universal superiority, effectiveness or learning success.

## LDR.Source:3 - Series, scope and limits

**Series and scope.** The Leadership product series develops self-direction and relations of leading and following through which people undertake responsible action and joint work. The first edition dated 12 October 2026 is its first admitted member and centres on joint contributions. This account connects that work to the person's own purposes and action, including ordinary work, change and development in organizations, communities and arrangements without a common employer. Negotiation, professional facilitation, human capability development, corporate governance, community management, strategy, implementation support and development practice retain their wider fields and direct methods. The four leadership patterns teach the selected constructions and their connections to intellectual and professional suppliers. The field explanation relates people's own purposes and capabilities, roles, influence, recognized initiative, authority and performed joint work; it does not absorb the supplying professions.


The contribution beyond the source organization-change frame is made explicit in the no-common-employer cases, ordinary-work non-use boundaries and qualified-AI alternatives. The same conditions are not presumed across all those settings. Authority, consent, capability, resources and evidence are reconstructed for the receiving use.

The following needs are deliberately not supplied by this framework: choosing an organization's whole strategy or development portfolio; creating every domain's methods; designing human instruction and assessment from scratch; constituting a community; engineering an AI's general competence; making legal or clinical determinations; and proving cultural or causal effects. The dependency returns explain how those results enter the leadership work.

Admit a later edition through an explicit decision when its relation to the actual source edition is established and the complete leadership language is qualified for this use. Retain the purpose of enabling responsible action and joint work through self-direction and relations of leading and following. Preserve independently useful entries, sufficient ordinary coordination, real authority and consent, actual capability and joint resource demands, and qualified human/AI allocation. Refinement, splitting or redistribution must preserve useful operations and qualified suppliers or provide qualified replacements. Correct false claims and mistaken boundaries. Source derivation alone does not admit an edition. Replacing this purpose with one of the wider neighboring practices identifies another series.

Review the affected admission or use when a governing distinction or relied-on source changes, a required contribution becomes unavailable, or use exposes a consequential failure. Loss of qualification calls for a warning and a decision about repair, withdrawal of recommendation or retirement. Superseded, unavailable or retired editions retain their historical membership while the series continues; a false admission claim requires correction. Retire the series by an explicit decision when its field and use will no longer be served or when repair after qualification loss is declined. Retirement ends its current belonging occurrences while preserving past facts; a later active collection requires a new constitution. A change of title, publication home, Suite membership or maintenance alone leaves the series identity unchanged. The constitution establishes no maintenance service, future edition or uninterrupted availability.

## LDR.Source:4 - Refresh and practical feedback

Reopen the affected contribution when a direct supplier changes a relied-on method or condition, when a professional alternative supplies a better answer at comparable effort, or when use exposes a missing operation. A change in AI competence, cost or permitted mandate can reopen the whole performer arrangement, not merely the tool choice.

Useful feedback identifies the receiving question, what the text enabled, the operation the practitioner still had to invent, the conditions of the attempted use and the consequence of that gap. A successful example does not settle unrelated settings; a failed prerequisite does not by itself refute a method used outside its conditions.

The Readme contains six ordinary practical entries: OWN-ACTION, NO-SHARED-DIRECTION, MISSING-HELP, WHOLE-AGREEMENT, UNANSWERED-QUESTION and the extended joint-use example JOINT-START. Use their situation and missing contribution to choose an entry; return to the complete Method for the explanation needed to adapt it.

# Management Accounting Principles Framework

**DocID:** `MA` within **FPF Library**.

**Edition:** [MA 1.0](#masources1---edition-record)

**Author:** Anatoly Levenchuk, with AI-assisted development and review

Management Accounting develops and uses economic knowledge of an organization's activity: what its results require, whom its resource use and commitments affect, and how different arrangements can sustain the intended work. It helps a controller, accountant or manager explain what happened, anticipate consequences, construct economically supportable changes, and arrange the use of information in decisions. A small account can be sufficient. A cost ceiling defines a condition; participants still need a feasible way of doing the work.

# Management Accounting Readme

## Practical entries

Begin with the work that needs to become understandable or possible. You may need an explanation of cost, an outlook, an economically supportable product or service arrangement, or information that helps people coordinate their decisions. These questions lead to different combinations of methods. Management Accounting connects the intended results, work, resource provision, monetary consequences and use of information; the responsible operating, engineering, financial and organizational practices contribute their own constructions and decisions.

These are selected connected examples. Enter where the explanation is missing; reuse an adequate model or account. The [Table of Contents](#table-of-contents) gives direct access to the methods, and the [Architectural Reference](#management-accounting-principles-framework-architectural-reference) explains the repertoire. You can ask an assisting agent to explain a pattern or comment on your case in the language of your work, without framework jargon. In MA.4:5, 4 identifies the pattern and 5 its section.

The calculations below are constructed cases under supplied operating, contractual and accounting premises. When applying them, obtain the applicable facts, reporting rules and decisions from the responsible practitioners.

### MA-E1 — An order is priced below reported average cost

- **Situation:** A proposed order looks loss-making in the standard report, but its resource demands, capacity conditions and payments may tell a different story.
- **Question:** What does accepting the work change, and can its payments and operating demands be met when required?
- **First useful result or blocker:** A usable resource and monetary model, then an operating comparison and the remaining capacity or funding question.
- **Start with:** [MA.1 - Build the Resource-Consumption and Cost Model](#ma1---build-the-resource-consumption-and-cost-model) when the dependencies are missing. Use an adequate model directly; enter MA.2 or MA.3 for a disputed capacity or assignment meaning.
- **Stop or return:** Supply the supported quantities and conditions to OPS.14 for the comparison. An unresolved schedule, financial term or funding question returns to the practice that can settle it.

1. **Recover what the order consumes.** In MA.1's test-order case, an order for 100 accepted units would bring 1,200 of receipts while the report assigns 1,500 of cost. Under the supplied one-attempt premise, six to nine setup hours plus twenty processing hours require 26–29 rig-hours. The operating account establishes twenty uncommitted hours and one obtainable ten-hour block. The interval already settles the one-block question; a more precise setup measurement would not change it.
2. **Attach payments through the actual supply arrangement.** [MA.2 - Explain the Cost and Use of Capacity](#ma2---explain-the-cost-and-use-of-capacity) keeps occupied hours, supplied blocks and payment changes distinct. The extra block costs 240; fourteen qualified staff-hours fit the supplied sixteen with unchanged pay. Materials cost 200 and the supplier 100, so the model returns 540 of additional payments. If the reported amount is instead disputed as a shared assignment, [MA.3 - Assign Shared Costs for the Stated Use](#ma3---assign-shared-costs-for-the-stated-use) recovers its tracing or convention. Changing that assignment does not establish a changed payment.
3. **Use the model for the receiving comparison and funding question.** With no displaced contribution and all other flows unchanged, OPS.14 compares 1,200 with 540 and obtains 660. The whole cash position answers a different question. Without the order, 500 would remain available through day 28 after all other receipts and obligations. Paying the order's 440 now leaves sixty, but the supplier's 100 is due on day 7 and the customer pays on day 28. The funding gap of forty remains despite the favorable comparison. An additional receipt of fifty common to both options before day 7 would close that gap without changing the 660 difference.
4. **Return a changed premise to the result it affects.** An eleven-hour setup makes demand 31 hours, beyond the supplied thirty. Reopen the resource model and operating feasibility; the earlier one-block result no longer applies. A later change in payment terms instead reopens the timed account. Neither requires rebuilding an unchanged part of the model.

### MA-E2 — Profit and cash movement disagree

- **Situation:** A positive reported result coexists with falling cash, and a lower unit-cost figure may be encouraging additional production.
- **Question:** Which differences belong to the accounts' meanings, and which actual action or use of the account may need to change?
- **First useful result or blocker:** A reconciled explanation of the accounts; if their use is the problem, a supported change to that use or the unresolved behavioral explanation.
- **Start with:** [MA.4 - Reconcile Operating, Reporting and Cash Accounts](#ma4---reconcile-operating-reporting-and-cash-accounts). Use [MA.9 - Design and Examine the Use of Management Accounting Information](#ma9---design-and-examine-the-use-of-management-accounting-information) directly when the monetary meanings are adequate and the unresolved question concerns behavior.
- **Stop or return:** A sufficient reconciliation can finish the request. A funding decision needs the whole timed cash position; changing rewards or authority needs the responsible organizational decision.

1. **Put the views on their actual event and policy bases.** MA.4's case starts with zero inventory, receivables and payables and includes only the transactions described below. Producing 100 units costs 200 in materials and 300 in resource supply, all paid; sixty units sell for 600, of which 400 is received and 200 remains receivable. Under the supplied full-production-cost policy, cost of sales is 300, closing inventory 200 and the reported result 300. Cash movement is −100.
2. **Carry the reconciliation to its user.** The internal account values inventory at materials only and expenses the 300 resource-supply payment, giving a result of 180 and inventory of eighty. Thus 300 − 200 inventory − 200 receivables and 180 − 80 inventory − 200 receivables both give −100. The 120 difference between results is retained production-resource cost, not another receipt. Preserve each view for its warranted use. If an event or policy is unresolved, obtain that answer from OPS.15 or the responsible reporting practice.
3. **Use the explanation to examine a consequential choice.** Suppose management considers producing 120 units with the same 300 resource payment and unchanged sales of sixty. MA.9 compares the account and the resulting resource use: unit cost falls from five to 4.5, but materials consume forty more in cash and unsold quantity rises from forty to sixty. This establishes the divergence the measure conceals. Whether an actual production increase followed that incentive, anticipated demand or another reason remains a separate question.
4. **Repair only the supported problem and return changed conditions.** If the account's use is the established problem, the responsible manager can stop treating lower unit cost alone as improved performance and consider demand, inventory and resource consequences together. Preserve the legitimate reporting account. Evidence of a warranted future requirement could instead support the extra production. A changed measurement or allocation basis returns to MA.4 or MA.3 before a performance comparison; [MA.7 - Explain a Cost or Margin Difference](#ma7---explain-a-cost-or-margin-difference) uses comparable meanings to separate the consequential difference from its still-unresolved cause.
5. **Carry the account into the next period when needed.** MA.4:5.2 starts from the remaining forty units and receivable, then derives the next closing balances. Results of 320 and 340 both connect to cash movement of 400. The changed result difference follows the release of earlier inventory cost; the explanation requires opening as well as closing values.

### MA-E3 — The forecast has become a resource negotiation

- **Situation:** One number is expected to serve as demand outlook, ambition, resource request and authorization, concealing the decision needed when they differ.
- **Question:** Which expectation should remain visible, and which actual action or resource decision could change the outlook?
- **First useful result or blocker:** Distinguishable expectations, ambitions, requests and authorizations, connected to the resource or management decision that matters.
- **Start with:** [MA.6 - Separate Forecasts, Targets and Resource Requests](#ma6---separate-forecasts-targets-and-resource-requests) for mixed meanings; [MA.5 - Construct and Update an Operating Forecast](#ma5---construct-and-update-an-operating-forecast) when the meanings are settled and the outlook needs construction or revision.
- **Stop or return:** Keep an adequate expectation visible. A resource request, its authorization and usable provision remain different results.

1. **Recover the use of each number.** MA.6's case has demand expected at 100 units, an ambition of 120, a request for provision covering a possible surge to 130, and authorization covering 110 under the supplied mix and scheduling assumptions. The authorization neither changes expected demand to 110 nor makes the ambition feasible.
2. **Connect the gap to the result that can resolve it.** MA.5 constructs or obtains the warranted demand outlook and its uncertainty. Its MA.5:5.1 example joins sixty booked units with forty further units estimated on a nonoverlapping basis; a sufficient supplied forecast can be used directly. Where conversion is missing, MA.1 and MA.2 relate demand to resource quantities and payments, using the adequate operating capacity account. The responsible manager can then decide about provision, scope or ambition. When the ambition or its comparison lacks a meaningful basis, [OPS.21](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops21---choose-operating-aims-targets-and-comparisons) constructs that missing result; an adequate supplied target can remain. Keep a proposed addition in the scenario where it occurs; do not make it available by editing the forecast.
3. **Propagate the actual change.** If a market action warrants a new expectation of 115, MA.5 updates that outlook and its assumptions. The gap against authorized capability is five units on the same basis; the target remains 120 and authorization 110 until their responsible participants change them. A fixed resource payment stays fixed under its terms even when demand changes.
4. **Use the later result without rewriting the earlier prediction.** Retain the earlier forecast's premises when learning from outcomes. MA.7 constructs comparable intermediate accounts to explain the difference. If product mix changed, MA.7:5.2 shows how to replace an aggregate usage term with mix and within-product usage; action taken in response may account for part of the observed change. If the reward or negotiation arrangement still suppresses unwelcome expectations, MA.9 examines that specific use and returns any wider organizational change to its responsible practice. The clarified accounts may already resolve the question. If the attained result still needs a performance judgement, [OPS.22](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops22---interpret-operating-performance-and-decide-the-response) examines target difficulty, changed conditions, action and joint effects before choosing a response. The [repair cooperative case (Engineering.Reference:7)](../Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#engineeringreference7---how-should-we-set-a-target-and-judge-a-miss-after-conditions-change) develops that continuation through an actual change in the local review rule.

### MA-E4 — Two customer cohorts share one paid service team

- **Situation:** A proposed cohort appears to contribute money, but it will share capacity and payment dates with an existing cohort.
- **Question:** What does adding it change after their demands are combined, and can the work and payments be met?
- **First useful result or blocker:** A joint resource account, the new cohort's future monetary difference and the whole dated cash position, with unresolved capacity or later flows kept visible.
- **Start with:** [MA.8 - Account for Customer and Product Economics Over Time](#ma8---account-for-customer-and-product-economics-over-time) when population or time is unclear. Use adequate supplied cohort quantities directly, then obtain missing resource and supply relationships through MA.1–MA.2.
- **Stop or return:** OPS.14 uses feasible future consequences for the operating comparison. An unknown obligation returns to FDM, a funding question to the relevant financial practice, and a sufficient supported account can finish the accounting request.

1. **Put both populations into the same calendar.** In this separate teaching case, the supplied active-customer quantities for months 2–4 are 80, 60 and 45 for the existing cohort, and 40, 20 and 10 for the proposed cohort. They are conditional scenario inputs. MA.8 explains how to obtain the calendar quantities from cohort age when they are not already supplied.

2. **Construct the shared resource demand.** Each cohort requires two setup hours per month plus 0.25 qualified service hour per active customer. The cohorts share 26 usable hours for an unchanged monthly payment of 240. One further nine-hour block can be obtained in each month for 180, paid at that month's start. Scheduling is supplied as feasible whenever the demands fit those quantities.

   | Calendar month | Existing cohort hours | Proposed cohort hours | Joint demand | Additional block needed |
   | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
   | 2 | 2 + 80 × 0.25 = 22 | 2 + 40 × 0.25 = 12 | **34** | **One** |
   | 3 | 2 + 60 × 0.25 = 17 | 2 + 20 × 0.25 = 7 | **24** | None |
   | 4 | 2 + 45 × 0.25 = 13.25 | 2 + 10 × 0.25 = 4.5 | **17.75** | None |

   Each cohort would fit the basic capacity alone, but their month-2 total requires the extra block. Both setups remain because the supplied work requires them. A proposed shared setup needs an operating basis before either is removed. The payment of 240 is for the common supply arrangement and appears once in the whole account.

3. **Distinguish the future difference from assigned and historical amounts.** The proposed cohort costs 600 to acquire before month 2. It pays 3 per active customer for service at month start and receives 15 per active customer at month end. Receipts total 15 × (40 + 20 + 10) = **1,050** and direct service payments total 3 × 70 = **210**. The added capacity payment is 180, so the future difference is **1,050 − 210 − 180 − 600 = 60**, with other flows unchanged.

   The existing cohort's acquisition payment of 2,000 is historical. A report assigns eight of team cost per active customer to the new cohort, totaling 560 over these months. MA.3 can explain that assignment; it is not another payment on top of the actual supply arrangements. The +60 concerns only this three-month alternative under the supplied conditions. Later flows and the responsible decision criteria remain outside that calculation.

4. **Restore the whole cash position at each payment date.** Without the new cohort, 900 would be available at every relevant date after all existing receipts and obligations, including the unchanged team payment. Acquisition reduces that position to 300. Add the new flows cumulatively to this baseline:

   | Date | Additional payment or receipt at this date | Whole cash position |
   | --- | ---: | ---: |
   | Before month 2: acquisition | −600 | **300** |
   | Month 2 start: service and block | −120 − 180 | **0** |
   | Month 2 end: receipts | +600 | **600** |
   | Month 3 start: service | −60 | **540** |
   | Month 3 end: receipts | +300 | **840** |
   | Month 4 start: service | −30 | **810** |
   | Month 4 end: receipts | +150 | **960** |

   Thus the positive difference coexists with zero cash buffer at the month-2 start. No unchanged payment is subtracted again after it has entered the baseline. MA.4 supplies a needed reconciliation to reported results, which can recognize amounts at different times.

5. **Reopen only the changed condition and its consequences.** Suppose evidence now bounds service effort for each active customer between 0.25 and 0.30 hour, without establishing one common rate for all customers. Add these individual bounds while keeping both setups. Joint demand is **34–40**, **24–28** and **17.75–20.5** hours. Month 2 may exceed the maximum supplied 35; month 3 may need the extra block above 26; month 4 fits.

   Obtain only the aggregate information that can resolve those thresholds, or a feasible revised operating arrangement. Precise measurement of every customer's effort is unnecessary if a supported aggregate bound settles the question. For a feasible month-2 branch, the future difference remains **60** when month 3 fits the basic supply, or becomes **−120** when month 3 also needs its 180 block. The month-2 receipts remain conditional while service feasibility is unresolved. Do not invent a second block or promise unchanged receipts for work that cannot be performed.

Constructing the cohort hours performs part of constructing this joint account. The combined capacity, dates and remaining uncertainty determine whether the whole account can be used, even when every local multiplication is correct.

### MA-E5 — The required economics has no supported design

- **Situation:** A product has a credible price and required margin, or a service has a funding ceiling, but no supported arrangement yet delivers the required result within those conditions.
- **Question:** Which changes in the offer, work and provision could produce an economically supportable arrangement?
- **First useful result or blocker:** Joint activity-design alternatives with their whole consequences and remaining conditions, or a supported conflict between the required result and available means.
- **Start with:** [MA.10 - Develop an Activity Design from an Economic Requirement](#ma10---develop-an-activity-design-from-an-economic-requirement). It connects the requirement to changeable dependencies and helps the responsible participants construct and examine alternatives.
- **Stop or return:** If supported alternatives already exist, use the adequate account and receiving comparison directly. Return an unresolved technical, market, resource or funding condition to the practice that can establish it.

MA.10:5 contrasts a product and support redesign with a funded service whose access and qualified capacity constrain the possible changes.

### MA-E6 — People need information before they can coordinate action

- **Situation:** People need to make a joint service commitment, but their existing information does not support the required coordination. A harmful metric effect need not have occurred.
- **Question:** What account and comparison must reach which participants in time for them to choose and carry out the needed action?
- **First useful result or blocker:** An information arrangement connecting the decision, participants, actions and timing, or an unresolved condition preventing its use.
- **Start with:** [MA.9 - Design and Examine the Use of Management Accounting Information](#ma9---design-and-examine-the-use-of-management-accounting-information). Its shared-service case exposes a capacity conflict before a promise is made.
- **Stop or return:** Retain an adequate arrangement. Use observations of whether people receive, understand and act on the information to identify a specific repair; return a missing capacity or authority decision to its responsible participants.

# Management Accounting Principles Framework Architectural Reference

## MA.Reference:1 - The working problem

An organization commits resources to obtain results for customers, members, service recipients or other participants. Its people must understand what can be sustained, which consequences an action changes, and what to do when the required result does not fit the available means. Management Accounting investigates these economic relationships and helps change the activity and its management. Producing an account is one important operation within that work.

A controller may need to explain why profit rose while cash fell. A product team may instead have an acceptable selling proposition and required return but no design that can deliver both. A public service may need to preserve access within a funding and staffing limit. A manager may need an arrangement in which an unfavorable forecast is reported early enough to change provision. These problems require different work: reconciliation, construction of alternatives, or design of information use. None is solved merely by having a more detailed statement of cost.

### MA.Reference:1.1 - Form the economic object from the activity and the question

Start with the result and the arrangement that produces it, or the arrangement being considered. Identify what counts as an accepted output, who uses it, which work produces and supports it, and which participants provide resources or carry obligations. A sale, an accepted delivery and a payment can be different events. An hour of qualified capacity, an hour actually occupied and an hour charged to a customer can be different quantities. Their relationships have to be established before a monetary total can explain the activity.

The economic object is selected through the unresolved relationship. A customer account groups acquisition, service, receipts and surviving obligations when these are needed to understand that relationship. A product account can include development, production, maintenance and withdrawal. A decision about one additional order can use a much smaller object while retaining the common resources and other work it could displace. The chart of accounts supplies useful observations and reporting classifications; it does not determine every object that a decision needs.

Choose units that preserve the consequential distinctions. Producing accepted units may require repeated attempts and rework; batches can require setups; active customers of different ages can require different service work. Several economic objects may draw on the same team; their separate accounts must retain that shared provision. Group similar work where its differences cannot change the conclusion, and split it when they can. Thus a change from outright sale to a maintained service can require new units for installed equipment, availability, interventions and surviving service duties. Renaming the old sales total would not recover that object.

Relate these quantities through the actual mechanisms and arrangements. Processing uses time and material; available capacity depends on qualification, calendars and maintenance; obtaining more capacity may require a whole shift or a new supplier. Contracts and institutional rules connect provision, transfer, obligations and payment. Reporting policies determine recognition and valuation for their stated uses. An allocation distributes an amount by a convention; it need not explain consumption or establish which payment an action can avoid.

Money makes some consequences comparable under specified prices, dates and valuation rules. It does not make customer usefulness, a participant's willingness to act, reported profit and available cash the same thing. Preserve material service, safety, access, environmental or other requirements in the form in which their responsible practice can establish them. An economic account can expose the resources required by such a condition without inventing a monetary value for satisfying it.

### MA.Reference:1.2 - Explain an arrangement and help construct a different one

For a known arrangement, work from outputs and activities through resource demand and provision to monetary consequences. Then interpret the result for its use: a historical explanation, a future comparison, a performance question or a funding requirement. The same activity can support several correct accounts. Reconcile their meanings when they meet; do not select one account as universally true and discard the others.

An economic requirement reverses the practical question. The required return, available funding or acceptable use of resources constrains a search for an arrangement; it does not specify that arrangement. A cost allowance cannot reveal which component to change, how to preserve service, or whether a supplier will accept a different commitment. Management Accounting helps the participants locate consequential dependencies, construct and evaluate combinations of changes, and discover when the requirement itself must be reconsidered. Use engineering, marketing and operating methods to develop and substantiate the proposed arrangement. The economic construction keeps its combined consequences visible.

This search is not confined to manufacturing. It can change what is offered, who does the work, the means used, the extent and timing of provision, or the terms connecting participants. A cheaper component may increase service work. A joint visit may reduce travel but prevent timely access. A transfer to a contractor may remove an internal payment while creating a continuing contractual obligation. The relevant whole must include the effects that can change the required judgement, including effects transferred to another participant.

A forecast and a requirement also have different grounds. A forecast estimates what follows from evidence and stated conditions. A target expresses an intended result. An authorization permits specified action. If the supported forecast misses the target, the gap can motivate inquiry and redesign; substituting the target for the forecast conceals the need for that work. If no credible arrangement meets the requirement, the useful result is the supported conflict and its consequences for the responsible choice.

### MA.Reference:1.3 - Make economic knowledge usable and revisable

The discipline also concerns how information enters action. People may use the same cost figure to price work, negotiate resources, judge performance or reward a team. These uses can require different comparisons and encourage different actions. Design the information and its use together: who can act, on what, by when, with which consequences visible? An account that explains the whole can still be a poor basis for attributing one participant's performance.

Economic knowledge is built from observations, models of work, applicable terms, and explicit judgements. Distinguish their grounds. Records can establish a payment; a contract can establish an obligation; an operational explanation and suitable observations can support a resource relationship. A calculated difference identifies where two accounts diverge, not by itself what caused behavior. A desired margin is a criterion chosen for a use, not an observed property of the product.

Practice changes this knowledge. A trial can expose omitted rework; a new contract can change which payment is avoidable; a revised service design can change the relation between customer count and workload. Compare the observation with what the model actually predicted under its stated conditions. Determine whether to correct data, change a relationship, narrow its applicability or replace the arrangement. Success under one set of conditions supports reuse there; generalizing to other scales, populations or forms of work requires support for the relationships that carry the inference.

The construction requires different intellectual operations. Select an abstraction that preserves the distinctions needed for the question: a common service-hour unit is adequate only while the work can draw on compatible provision. Synthesize contributions through their real relations: combining customer accounts must preserve their shared capacity and obligations. Generalize a supported relationship only to cases for which its necessary conditions hold. These operations determine what can be omitted, connected or reused, and what a changed condition would invalidate.

### MA.Reference:1.4 - The discipline's boundary and its collaborators

This framework covers economic explanation and construction for managing organizational activity, including the design and examination of accounting information in use. It therefore reaches from operational work to products, customers and commitments over time, and from observed consequences to proposed changes. It does not take over every professional task performed by a management accountant.

Investment valuation, financing and financial-risk treatment have their own financial methods. Tax, external reporting and legal duties require their applicable rules and competent practice. Engineering establishes technical and service realizations; marketing investigates the offer and its use; operating management establishes executable work and makes operating choices. Management Accounting participates in these constructions by developing the economic relationships and consequences they need. Referring to a collaborator does not discharge that contribution: obtain a usable result, connect its conditions, and return a changed premise to its owner.

This boundary permits both a small warranted calculation and a substantial joint redesign. It supplies no universal profit objective, optimal costing system or compulsory sequence through all the patterns. The receiving work determines which construction must be made and when it is sufficient.

## MA.Reference:2 - How the methods connect

Start from the explanation, decision or change of activity that must become possible, then work back to its missing contributions. A funding question needs receipts and payments at their dates. Obtaining those dates may require the workload, its resource demand and the actual supply or settlement arrangement. Keep an adequate supplied result; use its owning method when the result is missing or its assumptions no longer fit. This backward reading selects the necessary work, while the resulting inputs are then combined into the receiving account.

MA.1 constructs the resource-consumption and cost model when it is missing. It begins with work outputs and consequential resource dependencies, then relates quantities to supply, money and payment time. It also chooses detail: an interval can suffice when its variation cannot change the relevant threshold or comparison.

MA.2 and MA.3 are independent entries when capacity or shared assignment is the unresolved problem. Their results can improve MA.1's model, but neither is a mandatory stage in every model construction. MA.4 reconciles operating, reporting and cash accounts by carrying their opening balances through the relevant events to closing balances under each view's rules.

MA.5 constructs compatible demand inputs and carries them through resource relationships and balance movements to forecast the relevant outlook. MA.6 preserves its distinction from targets and resource decisions. MA.7 constructs intermediate accounts to explain a difference, including changed product mix, without treating arithmetic decomposition as causal evidence. MA.8 constructs cohort and product accounts across calendar periods and separates the whole history from a future choice. MA.9 designs and examines how information enters participants' decisions. MA.10 develops an economically supportable arrangement when a requirement is known but a suitable design is not.

Before joining results, align their population, period, quantities and account meanings. Units ordered, units produced and units delivered can differ. A cohort's second month is an age, not necessarily the calendar month used by another cohort. A resource-consumption value, a shared assignment and a payment can all describe the same work without being interchangeable amounts.

For a shared resource, add the demands that compete in the same calendar window before applying its usable-capacity, reserve or supply-block condition. Use the resulting supply arrangement to obtain payment once in the whole account. Two separately feasible demands can exceed shared capacity together; two allocated costs can also represent one unchanged payment. Preserve separate setups unless the operating model supports a replacement by shared work.

Carry the connected result into the receiving use. A population forecast supplies work quantities; those quantities supply resource demand; an obtainable supply action supplies its payment terms. A shortage returns to the operating decision about scope, schedule or provision. It does not create another resource block by calculation. MA.4 connects the resulting events and balances across valid account views. For an alternative comparison, isolate the changing future flows; for liquidity, restore all relevant flows and unchanged obligations in the whole cash position.

These methods can be used in different combinations. An established model can feed a forecast directly. A surprising variance can lead to a revised dependency or reveal a changed allocation. A harmful unit-cost target can require changing its use while keeping the report needed for another purpose. Enter the unresolved question and stop when the receiving use has an adequate result.

The accountant also performs work at several scopes at once. While calculating rig occupation, they can be deriving the order's resource demand and thereby constructing its resource account. The account's purpose determines what the calculation must include. Use [FPF B.1.5.EW — Recover How Constituent Actions Enact Encompassing Work][EW] when you cannot yet explain such a connection or locate the capability needed to perform it. MA.1:5.3 shows how an error between those scopes survives correct arithmetic. Reuse a connection you already understand.

The same relation appears in a joint customer account. Deriving one cohort's hours is already part of constructing the whole operating account, whose calendar window and shared-capacity condition constrain that derivation. The horizontal dependencies between results and this vertical contribution to the whole both matter: correct cohort calculations can still feed an incorrect combined account. The MA-E4 application follows both and reopens only the consequences of a changed effort bound.

Construction can change those connections. In MA.10, preserving an intended customer result may require changing both the product and its support arrangement. [SYSE.2][SYSE2] develops a system concept with its use, and [SYSE.8][SYSE8] develops the contributing provision arrangement. [MKT.2][MKT2] connects an offer with its use and price conditions. [ECO.2][ECO2], [ECO.3][ECO3] and [ECO.4][ECO4] address substitution, joint exchange terms and commitments when those are unresolved. MA.1 and MA.8 then reconstruct the proposed activity's resource and time consequences; they cannot simply retain the old per-unit cost. OPS.14 compares the resulting operating alternatives, OPS.19 resolves joint operating feasibility where needed, and [FIN.6][FIN6] supplies capital valuation when that is the receiving question.

The result of a part can revise the encompassing proposal. Unavailable maintenance capacity can invalidate a service promise and its expected receipts. Evidence that demand is lower can make an otherwise feasible design miss the required return. An acceptable economic arrangement can still lack cash before launch. Reopen the offer, design, scale, terms, criterion or funding question that the evidence actually changes. MA.9 connects the resulting account to a decision arrangement in which people can use and challenge it; it does not convert a conditional calculation into authority.

## MA.Reference:3 - A model that changes the next decision

In MA.1's constructed test-order case, 100 accepted units require 26–29 rig-hours. The supplied arrangement has 20 usable hours and one additional ten-hour block costing 240. Materials and supplier use add 300. The model therefore supplies 540 of additional payments, rather than the report's 1,500 assigned cost.

OPS.14 uses those quantities and the stated absence of displacement to compare the 1,200 receipt with 540, giving 660. Its funding question uses the whole timed cash position. Under the example's explicit baseline-cash premise, 440 is paid now, 100 is due on day 7 and the receipt arrives on day 28; a 40 day-7 funding gap remains. The favorable comparison and the unresolved funding are both useful results.

Other entries change different actions. MA.4 explains how inventory and receivables connect profit to cash. MA.6 preserves an expectation of 100, ambition of 120, request for provision covering 130 and authorization covering 110. MA.8 distinguishes the recovery of past acquisition or development payments from a new continuation choice. MA-E4 joins two cohorts before testing the common capacity and payment dates. A reader does not have to reconstruct the order model to use these methods.

## MA.Reference:4 - Correct use, evidence and effort

Begin by stating what explanation, activity design or use of information must become possible. For a connected use of the language, establish that the chosen methods supply that result, that their resource and monetary meanings agree where they connect, and that material time, uncertainty and supply conditions survive the connection. Use each pattern's substantive questions for the result it supplies; reopen the conditions changed by the current use.

A recognizable discrepancy is a reason to investigate. It is not proof that a proposed order should be accepted, that an allocated cost is avoidable or that a measure caused behavior. The worked examples establish reasoning under supplied facts. An actual conclusion needs adequate support for its resource relationships, terms, observations and causal claims.

The gain is an explained decision or a workable change in activity. Its cost includes obtaining the needed knowledge and developing and maintaining the proposed arrangement. Reuse adequate models and observations. Increase detail where a plausible difference could change the answer or its required assurance.

A commercial example supplies no universal monetary objective. An internal or public service can use these accounting methods while obtaining its intended result and choice criteria from the responsible practice. Forecast and performance arrangements must also be examined from the affected participants' positions, rather than assuming a single account expresses every interest.

## MA.Reference:5 - Why this organization of methods

The repertoire follows distinguishable work within the field. Understanding what activity consumes calls for a model of work and provision. Understanding different monetary representations calls for assignment and reconciliation. Anticipating future consequences calls for supported demand and resource relationships. Learning from differences calls for comparable accounts and a separate inquiry into causes. Finding an arrangement that can meet an economic requirement calls for construction and comparison of alternatives. Making this knowledge effective calls for an appropriate use of information in participants' work.

These families explain the pattern boundaries. MA.1 develops the resource and cost model; capacity and shared assignments merit independent entries in MA.2 and MA.3 because they can be unresolved even when the surrounding model is adequate. MA.4 connects views through events and balances. MA.5 constructs an outlook, while MA.6 prevents that outlook from silently becoming a target or authorization. MA.7 explains differences. MA.8 handles the time and population relations that a single period or average customer can conceal. MA.9 concerns information in an action arrangement. MA.10 concerns the economic construction of an activity arrangement. Each can begin from adequate results supplied by the others.

The separation matters in practice. More accurate multiplication cannot recover a missing setup. A reconciled variance cannot establish its cause. A forecast cannot authorize a resource request. A target cost cannot supply a design. A better design cannot make an inappropriate performance attribution fair. These are different missing contributions, not stages that every case must traverse.

The families intersect broader professional work without requiring duplicate methods. Pricing needs an adequate offer and market account as well as economic consequences. A make-or-buy choice needs feasible provision and exchange terms. An investment needs a usable project design, cash consequences and financial valuation. Management Accounting's contribution changes with each use; the financial, engineering or operating decision retains its own criteria and authority. Internal assignments and transfer charges may support a legitimate account while their effects on joint behavior require MA.9. A tax transfer-price judgement has a different governing basis.

A stable simple report is adequate when it preserves the distinctions its use needs. A detailed activity model, forecasting system or wider organizational change earns its effort through a consequential improvement in the receiving work. A new result can also require a new decomposition: a maintained service may replace a unit-sale model with linked installed-base, intervention and obligation accounts. Preserve adequate parts, but derive the revised connection from the activity rather than forcing the new question into the old report.

## MA.Reference:6 - Sources, qualifications and changed conditions

Internal and externally required accounts serve different uses. An account must retain capacity thresholds and the acquisition or scale assumptions that change its resource and monetary consequences. Changing an expectation is distinct from deciding about resources. Cost models remain useful when their meaning fits the receiving decision. Revenue uncertainty calls for warranted scenarios; unit economics, ROI and ROMI need their actual definitions and cannot be treated as interchangeable labels.

IMA's managerial-cost-model guidance contributes resource dependencies and a use-driven choice of model detail. Bragg and Caspari supply historical constraint-accounting cases that expose the difference between assigned cost, capacity and changed payments. The relevant TameFlow capacity distinctions are used with adequate OPS operating results; elapsed flow time alone does not identify the constraint.

Bogsnes and the continuing Beyond Budgeting principles shape MA.5–MA.6's separation of expectation, ambition and resource allocation. The wider organizational proposal is an alternative whose value depends on the actual problem. Forecasting: Principles and Practice supplies the construction and qualification of missing forecast inputs in MA.5. ACCA's intermediate-account and life-cycle explanations support the changed-composition and product-time constructions in MA.7–MA.8. The customer-model sources used in MA.8 qualify population, horizon and continuation assumptions. Their contribution is to avoid an unwarranted universal formula, not to require every account to adopt one predictive model.

IMA's 2014 *Conceptual Framework for Managerial Costing* is a historical foundation for relating operational quantities to decision use; its scope is managerial costing, not the whole profession. The 2023 *Global Management Accounting Principles* locates economic information in business models, resource allocation and management action. These are complementary grounds, not evidence that one model or professional map exhausts the field. ACCA's target-costing explanation supplies the reverse question developed in MA.10: required economics can motivate changes across design, production and support. The method treats the requirement as conditional and checks the actual arrangement rather than assuming a target is attainable.

Use the source qualifications in the relevant pattern when adapting its method. Reopen affected knowledge and uses when resource behavior, contract terms, reporting rules, population, intended result or decision arrangements change. A changed physical relationship calls for a revised model; a changed reporting rule can call for reconciliation while leaving that relationship intact; a new participant or promise can require a different economic object.

For source qualifications, citation and edition information, see the [Sources and Edition Notes](#management-accounting-principles-framework-sources-and-edition-notes).
