## Management.Reference:1 - The work this Suite serves

Management concerns choosing and sustaining the direction, commitments and provision of a collective undertaking, and changing them when the results or conditions warrant it. The undertaking may be a company, public service, professional practice, temporary collaboration or voluntary community. Its participants can have different purposes and decision rights. A shared employer is unnecessary; an actual basis for making and relying on a contribution is necessary.

Use this Suite when a worthwhile direction, an accepted promise, available means and ongoing work do not yet fit together. It helps obtain a supported commitment and its workable continuation: what can be done, for whom, by which contributions, with which authority and resources, and what must be reconsidered if a consequential condition changes. Retaining a sufficient arrangement, narrowing a promise or declining it can be useful results.

When an organization or another established system is the target, management's engineering contribution concerns that system: practitioners arrange and change the Work, authority, resources and commitments through which it can function. A changed allocation that establishes effective access or a new work commitment changes the system's state even if its organization chart remains the same. A voluntary community or temporary collaboration requires its own account of the system and whole, if any, that is being changed. System-level design, realization and qualification therefore remain relevant to ongoing management as well as to reorganization. OCE develops the deliberate construction of organizational relations and capability; it does not replace the other management fields or make every management use an OCE project. This organizational specialization is described by the Management Suite. The broader Engineering edition connects to it without repeating OCE in its direct roster.

The intended readers are people and capable assisting agents who make, support or examine management decisions. Relevant professional knowledge and powers remain necessary for the acts that require them. A practitioner can obtain a specialist result instead of learning to produce it. Follow [Using FPF Library](../../USING-FPF.md) to find the needed contribution and read its full pattern, including its conditions and worked cases.

## Management.Reference:2 - Constituent fields and their contributions

The Suite connects the following twelve DPFs. Each develops knowledge and reusable practices for a particular management subject. The entry patterns below show how their results participate in the larger work; they are selected entries, not a required sequence.

| Constituent field | Its own question and useful entry | Connection to the management whole |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Strategy (STR)](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) — STR | Which contribution and direction are worth pursuing, and which commitments remain defensible? [STR.8](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str8---relate-capabilities-dependencies-business-models-and-initiatives), [STR.11](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str11---select-strategy-portfolio-commitments-and-assumptions) and [STR.16](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str16---construct-a-feasible-portfolio-with-shared-or-branch-specific-support) connect capability, choices and a feasible portfolio. | Direction selects the work worth supporting. Operating, financial and participation conditions can defeat an attractive portfolio or change its scope. |
| [Operations Management (OPS)](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) — OPS | How can the needed production or service be arranged, provided and revised, and what can ongoing work admit, continue and deliver? [OPS.Reference:1](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#opsreference1---start-from-a-difficulty-in-continuing-operation) explains the field and [OPS.11.1](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops111---construct-and-reconcile-operating-models-across-scales) develops the operating construction. [OPS.10](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops10---qualify-operating-capacity-under-variability), [OPS.13](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops13---align-commitments-resources-and-service-outcomes) and [OPS.22](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops22---interpret-operating-performance-and-decide-the-response) qualify capability, agree service and interpret performance. | Its capacity and service results constrain promises; actual delivery and unresolved obligations return to the responsible management decision. |
| [Organization Administration (ADM)](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) — ADM | Which institutional condition must a participant actually receive, and under which rules? [ADM.8](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm8---establish-and-exercise-the-required-permission-for-an-administrative-action), [ADM.9](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm9---provide-a-usable-administrative-result) and [ADM.11](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm11---join-providers-around-the-administrative-result) connect permission, usable provision and providers. | A selected undertaking needs effective access, payments and other enabling services at the required time. A record of provision can be insufficient for the participant's work. |
| [Corporate Governance (CGOV)](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) — CGOV | Which corporate powers, rights and duties govern the act? [CGOV.3](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov3---establish-authority-for-corporate-appointments-removals-and-decisions), [CGOV.11](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov11---make-and-record-a-corporate-decision) and [CGOV.13](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov13---monitor-corporate-performance-and-require-an-account) connect authority, decision and accountable response. | Corporate undertakings need acts made by eligible participants under applicable rules. This is the corporate branch; a voluntary community uses its own mandate. |
| [Management Accounting (MA)](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) — MA | How do activity, resources and money relate, and what arrangement could meet the economic requirement? [MA.1](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma1---build-the-resource-consumption-and-cost-model), [MA.4](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma4---reconcile-operating-reporting-and-cash-accounts) and [MA.10](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma10---develop-an-activity-design-from-an-economic-requirement) connect resource and monetary accounts to activity design; [MA.9](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma9---design-and-examine-the-use-of-management-accounting-information) designs and examines the use of information. | These relationships explain and constrain operating and financial choices. An unmet economic requirement can call for different offers, products, processes or provision; information use can alter what participants choose and report. |
| [Corporate Finance (FIN)](CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) — FIN | How do the activity's financial relations constrain value and payment capacity, and which investment, financing or group arrangement should change? [FIN.Reference](CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#finreference1---problem-frame) explains the subject; [FIN.2](CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin2---assess-liquidity-and-funding-needs-by-date) supplies dated cash; [FIN.9](CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin9---compare-capital-investments-and-allocations) compares capital uses; [FIN.10](CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin10---design-financing-instruments-and-terms) constructs financing terms; [FIN.23](CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin23---construct-financing-arrangements-across-group-entities) connects financing across entities; [FIN.16](CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin16---prepare-a-finance-recommendation-and-return-it-for-a-decision) makes the resulting recommendation usable. | Value and funding conditions constrain corporate commitments. The same money, dates and outstanding obligations must survive the joins to strategy and operations. |
| [Marketing (MKT)](MARKETING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) — MKT | Which customer result and offer are useful, obtainable and commercially continuable? [MKT.Reference](MARKETING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mktreference1---problem-frame---useful-offers-in-actual-customer-situations) explains the field; [MKT.1](MARKETING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mkt1---qualify-a-market-problem-and-differences-between-customers) obtains customer differences; [MKT.11](MARKETING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mkt11---align-promises-partners-and-execution) constructs supported promises and distribution arrangements; [MKT.14](MARKETING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mkt14---develop-and-change-a-programme-for-selected-customer-organisations) connects customer programmes. | Customer evidence can change direction; provider capability and terms limit the offer; actual customer use can reopen the promise or commercial model. |
| [Customization and Productization Management (CUST)](CUSTOMIZATION-AND-PRODUCTIZATION-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) — CUST | Which client differences fit an existing offering, need a local answer or a changed family, or should be declined? CUST.1 connects client work, repeatable offerings and continuing obligations; CUST.3 constructs an offering family and CUST.8 changes it while existing obligations continue. | Local application can change the general offering, its permitted variations and its provision. Those changes constrain promises, operating capacity and the burden of maintaining the offering. |
| [Engineering Asset Management (EAM)](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) — EAM | What value should be obtained through engineered assets over time? [EAM.10](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam10---compare-engineered-asset-portfolio-combinations), [EAM.11](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam11---time-asset-interventions-and-manage-dependencies) and [EAM.12](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam12---integrate-specialist-results-for-an-asset-recommendation-or-decision) connect portfolio choices, intervention timing and qualified specialist results. | Asset options compete for funding and operational availability. Service need and technical evidence constrain the management choice; engineering and maintenance supply their own results. |
| [Leadership (LDR)](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) — LDR | How can people direct their own action, develop joint direction and participation, and obtain feasible contributions? [LDR.Reference:1.6](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldrreference16---direct-ones-own-contribution-and-development) explains the personal branch; [LDR.5](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldr5---develop-joint-direction-and-participation) develops direction and participation when these are not yet adequate. [LDR.1](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldr1---obtain-and-continue-the-leadership-contribution-needed-for-joint-work), [LDR.2](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldr2---agree-feasible-joint-contributions) and [LDR.4](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldr4---prepare-a-proposal-for-decision-and-first-use) connect capable help, feasible agreement and a proposal's passage to decision and first use. | A proposal becomes usable through actual contributions and legitimate decisions. A title or an attractive plan leaves that work unanswered. |
| [Community Management (CB)](COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) — CB | How can useful participation, relationships and common contributions be arranged and sustained? [CB.7](COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb7---prepare-and-sustain-distributed-organising), [CB.9](COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb9---provide-for-community-work-and-agree-its-terms) and [CB.13](COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb13---establish-a-workable-mandate-for-shared-decisions) connect organising, provision and shared mandates. | Community purposes and voluntary terms constrain commitments and support. Participants' experience can require changes in the offer, burden, representation or continuation. |
| [Organization Change Engineering (OCE)](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) — OCE | Which organizational relations and capability need deliberate construction or change? [OCE.3](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce3---generate-and-compare-organization-concepts), [OCE.4](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce4---design-an-organizations-contribution-architecture) and [OCE.9](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce9---realize-a-bounded-organization-capability-increment) connect concepts, contribution architecture and realization. | Specialization, information, decision rights, participation and support determine which commitments can be met. Their consequences can reopen the arrangement or the commitment. |

Corporate Governance and Corporate Finance retain their corporate subject and institutional prerequisites. Other undertakings use the applicable financial and governing practices for their setting. Membership of the Suite does not make every constituent necessary in every case.

Community Management includes valued relationships, mutual help and enjoyable shared activity. Commercial return is only one possible concern. Independent people carrying a practice need not form a managed community or delegate any common authority. Use CB for an actual participation or common-work question; the wider cultural question belongs to [FPF C.36.RP](../../FPF-Spec.md#c36rp---sustain-and-renew-shared-ways-of-working).

## Management.Reference:3 - What makes these fields a whole

The common subject is the management of an undertaking through compatible direction, commitments, provision and performance. Its constituent contributions constrain the same acts and consequences. A customer promise sets work requirements; an operating answer tests whether those requirements can be met; a resource account explains the demand and payments; a governing act supplies the required authority. A strategic comparison must retain those conditions when selecting the undertaking. The relationships run back as well: a failed service, changed resource condition or refused contribution can require a different promise or direction.

For example, [MKT.11](MARKETING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mkt11---align-promises-partners-and-execution) carries an offer into a real supply answer and returns an unsupported promise for revision. [OPS.13](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops13---align-commitments-resources-and-service-outcomes) preserves existing obligations while comparing scope, time or resource changes. [MA.1](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma1---build-the-resource-consumption-and-cost-model) explains the resource consumption that both uses require; [FIN.2](CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin2---assess-liquidity-and-funding-needs-by-date) establishes the corporation's dated funding position where that question is live. [CGOV.11](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov11---make-and-record-a-corporate-decision) makes the corporate decision when its conditions apply, while [CB.13](COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb13---establish-a-workable-mandate-for-shared-decisions) supplies a community mandate. [LDR.2](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldr2---agree-feasible-joint-contributions) obtains responses to the same complete proposal and returns changed contributions to the parties affected by them. These are connections between complete Methods, with different results and sources of authority.

Economic inquiry also runs from a requirement towards a proposed arrangement. [MA.10](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma10---develop-an-activity-design-from-an-economic-requirement) connects the required result and economic conditions to changes in the offer, product, process and provision, returning each technical or organizational question to the practice able to answer it. Cost, capacity and payment timing are evaluated for the jointly changed arrangement. That comparison can revise the proposal or its requirement; a changed activity can also require different resource units, forecasts or uses of accounting information.

[Customization and Productization Management (CUST)](CUSTOMIZATION-AND-PRODUCTIZATION-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) connects differences encountered in client work to a maintainable local answer or repeatable offering. A successful local result can depend on exceptional expertise, restricted material or a configuration that cannot be supported elsewhere. CUST.1 explains the connected Method; CUST.2–CUST.8 are also directly usable when only their particular result is missing.

An offering family constructed through CUST.3 constrains which variations MKT.11 may promise. A qualified delivery arrangement from CUST.6 supplies OPS.13 with its demand on performers, partners and support. CUST.7 uses the full resource and economic comparison of MA.8 to examine growth in demand and variety, including adaptation and continuing maintenance. These consequences can require a different family or a narrower promise. CUST.8 connects a changed general offering to the transitions still owed to existing clients. A successful new configuration does not erase those obligations.


At the portfolio scale, [STR.16](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str16---construct-a-feasible-portfolio-with-shared-or-branch-specific-support) constructs shared or separate support while preserving the purposes and evidence of each branch. [STR.8](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str8---relate-capabilities-dependencies-business-models-and-initiatives) supplies result dependencies, [STR.14](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str14---reconcile-simultaneous-strategic-work-across-horizons-and-scales) reconciles competing work across horizons, and [STR.11](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str11---select-strategy-portfolio-commitments-and-assumptions) carries the supported comparison into an authorized commitment. For an asset-dependent undertaking, [EAM.12](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam12---integrate-specialist-results-for-an-asset-recommendation-or-decision) receives the specialist results needed for the asset answer; it returns a missing engineering, operating or financial premise to its supplier.

These connected Methods help practitioners construct and revise **jointly supportable management commitments**. A good direction, a valid budget and an achievable local schedule can still be incompatible when they rely on the same unavailable resource, an unmade decision or a participant who has not agreed. Examining the whole means retaining these shared conditions and their consequences through the actual decision.

The whole also connects knowledge to practice. Knowledge of demand, resource consumption, authority, incentives and participation informs the construction and criticism of commitments. Results of practice can expose a bad assumption, an inappropriate measure or a missing condition. [MA.9](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma9---design-and-examine-the-use-of-management-accounting-information) develops that return for the use of accounting information; [OPS.22](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops22---interpret-operating-performance-and-decide-the-response) for operating performance; [STR.12](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str12---observe-signals-to-continue-or-reconsider-strategic-direction-and-commitments) for strategic premises; and [CB.10](COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb10---understand-the-value-of-participation-and-cultural-work) for participation. A changed observation first reopens the claim it bears on. A general causal conclusion needs the corresponding inquiry and evidence.

This Suite uses those existing full Methods for the connections it describes. This Architectural Reference helps a reader find and understand their joint use; the linked patterns supply the operations, cases and limits needed to perform it.

[Operations management](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#opsreference15---relate-management-practice-to-its-control-arrangements) realizes control in the common sense developed by FPF C.43: it organizes and revises how the undertaking obtains its results. The discipline also develops and designs the operating arrangements. Its established name remains Operations Management; the name identifies the field, while a particular control claim identifies what is influenced and how. Organizational commitments, participation and decision rights remain part of that explanation. The [2024 Operations Management editorial statement](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mnsc.2024.opmstmt.v70.n5) documents the field's concern with producing and delivering goods and services and the resources used across that work; it is used here for disciplinary scope, not as proof that any one management method is current best practice.

The connection also requires a temporal arrangement. FPF C.43:4.5.1 explains how to preserve recurring work while a separately timed response changes. OPS.13:4.5 chooses periodic review, event signaling or both; OPS.10.2 fits the response with preparation, recovery and already committed resources. A changed event should neither wait for a regular meeting when that loses the useful response nor silently reset every continuing obligation. Revise the affected relationship and the commitments that actually depend on it.

For the common reasoning that connects observation, choice, action and subsequent revision, apply FPF C.43. The organizational specialization retains differences that a generic feedback diagram can hide. OPS.21 distinguishes a forecast from a goal and commitment; OPS.10.2 constructs a schedule under shared capacity and precedence; OPS.14 compares the economic consequences of actual alternatives; OPS.22 interprets performance and selects the response. STR.8 connects contributions to an attainable direction, while STR.9 and STR.12 compare transitions and return changed premises to the strategic choice.

The economic comparison starts from the actual configuration but also asks which attainable use of means is displaced. It includes payments, capacity, timing and the consequences for participants under the receiving decision's criteria. Organizational authority and participation explain how a selected continuation can become work. A technically feasible instruction, a positive financial contribution and an accepted commitment therefore answer different questions. Development adds a further receiving result. FPF C.43:4.8 connects intervention in a working Method, capability, provision or the means of development to changed future possibilities. C.40.OD supplies the whole open-ended construction, C.40.JD joins its actual contributions, and C.40.NP derives further attainable problems from a result. A development adviser can apply PSDA.14 and PSDA.15 in the Decision Design Principles Framework to form advice and reconsider it from its actual use. This helps an organization choose between obtaining a service, developing its performers, changing their Method or changing the way development is organized. The economic comparison includes the attained repertoire, transition, displaced work and retained external help; maintaining current operations within target is a different sufficient result where no further development is intended.

### Management.Reference:3.1 - Organizational construction and maintenance use

Management includes constructing and changing organizational arrangements as well as directing work through adequate existing ones. OCE develops this constituent subject and has its full home in the Management Suite. Its organizational target connects the construction to direction, commitments, authority, provision and performance. An asset-dependent undertaking also needs maintenance policy and programme work; it obtains the full MNT Methods through [Engineering (Engineering.Reference:0)](../Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#engineeringreference0---engineering-specialization-and-maintenance). This use retains the maintenance field's own failure, condition and functioning questions.

**Organizational construction.** OCE connects knowledge of specialization, coordination, information, incentives and participation to the deliberate construction of organizational relations and capability. OCE.3 and OCE.4 construct interacting organization choices, rather than accepting an organization chart as the complete answer. OCE.5 and OCE.6 distinguish established positions from assignments and other enabling relations. OCE.9 realizes a bounded contribution; OCE.13 and OCE.14 return consequences to the choice of relations.

Those relations determine which management commitments can be made and sustained. A direction requiring independent acceptance needs an arrangement that supports independent judgement. A promise requiring the same specialist for incompatible work needs a different allocation, support or promise. Changed demand, authority or participation can reopen the organization design; the design's consequences can reopen direction and provision. Together with Strategy, Operations, Administration, Governance and Leadership, this contribution supports jointly feasible commitments rather than a set of separately plausible plans.

Engineering uses the same organizational knowledge and constructions to obtain functioning systems: OCE.7 coordinates organization and product or service architectures, while OCE.9 and OCE.11 connect realization to the conditions of use and continuing service. These contributions remain engineering through their organizational specialization in Management; this does not require a second direct inclusion of OCE in the broader Engineering edition. OCE does not cover all Organization Development, nor does a management task require organizational redesign whenever it uses this Suite.

**Maintenance.** MNT's subject is preserving or restoring required functioning, especially for physical and cyber-physical equipment in use. Maintenance engineering and maintenance management have distinct results within this connected field. The technical failure account constrains the policy and response; support, access and service conditions constrain which technically plausible response can be performed.

MNT.2 makes this connection within policy construction. A useful warning must leave time for detection, interpretation, support, access and intervention. MNT.5 and MNT.7 establish the support and operating arrangement needed by that response. MNT.8–MNT.11 retain separate protection, intervention, functioning and resumed-use results. MNT.12 and MNT.13 connect actual configuration and comparable failure history to choices about policy, support or programme. A recurring support delay calls for a different response from a failure mechanism that the task cannot address.

In management work, this field connects the operating promise to maintenance demands, obtainable provision and a programme that can change on evidence. It receives qualified capacity from Operations and relevant resource, funding and administrative results from their own practices. Its maintenance knowledge prevents an apparently affordable programme from promising unsupported availability. In Engineering, that same knowledge and practice constrain maintainability, realization and restored functioning; evidence from use can reopen the design. Neither relationship depends on every undertaking having equipment to maintain.

Maintenance does not absorb Engineering Asset Management. For a single pump, selecting a policy or intervention to preserve required functioning is a maintenance result. Comparing continued use, renewal, replacement, repurposing or withdrawal by value, costs, risks and service effects is an asset-management result. Conversely, coordinating a fleet maintenance programme remains MNT.13. Scale, the word replacement and the practitioner's job title do not decide the subject; one case can require both contributions.

OCE is a constituent because constructing organizational relations and capability participates in the same organizational subject as direction, commitments, authority and provision. MNT's whole subject instead connects failure and condition knowledge to maintaining required functioning. Keeping MNT in Engineering, with its full Methods available to management practitioners, preserves every policy, support and programme connection described here. The manager can perform a maintenance Method with the required capability; using an external discipline does not mean outsourcing the work. Dividing either complete repertoire into separate engineering and management products would obscure the interactions within OCE's organization choices and MNT's policy and response.

The cross-Suite arrangement requires users to preserve the conditions on both contributions. A changed organizational premise can affect both system realization and management commitments; a changed maintenance premise can affect both functioning and the service programme. Each Suite explains its own receiving connections. A user following a changed premise may therefore need both accounts, although the full Method remains in one description.

## Management.Reference:4 - Development, shared support and effective commitments

Management can support the development of an undertaking, its participants and the practices they use. Its contribution is to make the selected work supportable and keep its commitments connected. The development question remains what new problems become attainable and what changes make that possible; a sound allocation does not answer it. [FPF C.40.OD](../../FPF-Spec.md#c40od---construct-and-continue-open-ended-development) supplies the open-ended construction, [FPF C.40.JD](../../FPF-Spec.md#c40jd---develop-a-way-its-holder-and-its-provision-together) connects a way of obtaining a result with the development of its holder and provision, and [FPF C.40.NP](../../FPF-Spec.md#c40np---continue-from-a-result-to-new-attainable-problems) continues from a useful result to another worthwhile attainable problem. A bounded management decision can finish while that development continues.

### Management.Reference:4.1 - Shared support connects branches without merging their purposes

Research, product provision, human development, infrastructure work and community work can each be worth undertaking while competing for the same performers. Ranking each direction separately can promise incompatible work or charge the same common provision several times. The management whole needs both the reasons for pursuing the branches and a feasible account of their shared means.

[STR.16](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str16---construct-a-feasible-portfolio-with-shared-or-branch-specific-support) constructs shared versus branch-specific support, joint demand and feasible combinations. It preserves scientific and editorial ends and decisions, and can use an adequate existing Strategy result directly. For a development provider, the comparison can include its own development, a shared Method library, independent scientific contributions, business-to-consumer and business-to-business provision, client projects and work involving people, AI and communities alongside current obligations. These are possible branches of one provider's portfolio, not a required organization of development.

A shared office is one possible realization of a common contribution. The common part must remain usable for each receiver; each branch still needs its subject interpretation, acceptance and any distinct support. Shared maintenance can save repeated work while adding coordination, waiting, adaptation and a common failure exposure. Provision within each branch can be preferable when specialist criteria, confidentiality, independent judgement or incompatible calendars make sharing unsuitable. Either arrangement can use distributed performers instead of an office.

The provider's remit is a separate choice: a service specializing in development can obtain other subject expertise externally and still supply its own contribution. C.40.JD:4.5 explains that distinction; STR.16:4.3 develops the sharing comparison. [FPF C.32.MWA.PP](../../FPF-Spec.md#c32mwapp---construct-and-compare-method-performance-and-provision-arrangements) supplies the performance and provision architecture when those arrangements still need construction; [OCE.4](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce4---design-an-organizations-contribution-architecture) supplies an organizational contribution architecture when an organization boundary must be designed. Neither a portfolio nor an office name establishes the needed capability or authority.

Demands on the same performer must be reconciled against that performer's availability, even when that person fills several roles. A research branch's assigned cost share is also different from a payment avoided by cancelling it. STR.16:4.4 retains those distinctions and the actual time windows. A result dependency is another relation: a product needs new research only where a specific receiving operation cannot proceed with an adequate existing or alternative result. Independent inquiry can remain worth supporting on its own grounds.

Independent mathematical inquiry with no material shared dependency need not acquire a portfolio or office merely to use a development Method. The management comparison stops with the sufficient bounded decision and reopens the affected combination when a shared condition changes. When continued development is part of the purpose, its next problem comes from the development construction rather than from a requirement to perpetuate the management project.

### Management.Reference:4.2 - A proposal reaches work through judgement, decisions and contributions
Sometimes the direction and participants are still being formed. [LDR.5](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldr5---develop-joint-direction-and-participation) connects participants' experience and purposes with subject inquiry, a direction they can consider, and the responsibilities they actually undertake. A changed technical premise returns to Strategy or the relevant subject method; changed participation returns to a workable contribution or another direction. [LDR.Reference:1.6](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldrreference16---direct-ones-own-contribution-and-development) explains how a person's own purpose, present commitments and learning shape their next action. When direction and participation are already adequate, the corresponding agreement or preparation Method can be used directly.

An accepted strategy does not supply all the contributions needed to enact it. Telling people about the strategy can leave both a substantive objection and an incompatible promise unanswered. The connection is through the participants' actual work, authority and response to the same proposal.

[LDR.1](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldr1---obtain-and-continue-the-leadership-contribution-needed-for-joint-work) obtains and continues a missing leadership contribution. [LDR.2](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldr2---agree-feasible-joint-contributions) negotiates complete feasible contributions. [LDR.4](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldr4---prepare-a-proposal-for-decision-and-first-use) prepares a proposal through decision, commitments, a mutually understood start and first useful work. This last contribution includes what is sometimes called *propitka*: relevant trusted judgement and examination of consequences can change the proposal before commitment, and first use tests what the agreement actually provided. An adviser may help a participant judge the proposal without having authority to decide or commit on that participant's behalf.

When a subject question still needs a useful answer, [FPF B.5.SD](../../FPF-Spec.md#b5sd---construct-a-useful-answer-through-substantive-discussion) supplies its construction through substantive discussion. An unsupported inference needs subject reasoning; a real disadvantage can require another proposal; incompatible contributions need an agreement that can be performed. These returns do not make agreement a test of technical truth or make a technically sound proposal acceptable to every participant. Informed refusal and a decision under a valid non-consensual rule remain different results.

LDR.4 supplies the whole passage when that is missing. One of the other Methods can be used directly when only its contribution is needed. A voluntary community need not share an employer: [CB.13](COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb13---establish-a-workable-mandate-for-shared-decisions) can establish the shared mandate, while participants retain powers they have not delegated. In a corporation, the applicable governance acts retain their own conditions. A person or AI may perform an authorized contribution; fluent analysis or a simulated preference does not supply another party's consent. Ordinary sufficient coordination needs no special preparation campaign.

The first useful handover supplies evidence at its actual scope. Continued help can remain part of the arrangement; success with that help does not show independent mastery. When the first use fails, LDR.4 returns the missing explanation, capability, means, access, authority or Method to its supplier instead of prescribing another announcement.

### Management.Reference:4.3 - Connected documents express compatible results

A provider may need a concept, strategy, project architecture and programmes for its own development and its capacity to help clients. Those documents describe different subjects and decisions. Their usefulness depends on the compatible contributions they describe, rather than on adopting the same layout or copying one framework's contents table.

[FPF C.40.OD:4.8](../../FPF-Spec.md#c40od48---make-the-way-reconstructible-in-further-use) identifies the decisions and Methods that must remain available at the point of use. [STR.6](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str6---construct-strategic-option-families-or-develop-reusable-material-for-strategic-exploration) supplies complete strategic alternatives; [STR.8:4.2a](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str842a---explain-why-the-proposed-changes-would-work-together) explains why proposed changes and already available contributions can work together; [STR.11](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str11---select-strategy-portfolio-commitments-and-assumptions) supplies bounded commitments. This connects the reason for a result to the actions that could obtain it, without turning every constituent action into a new initiative or treating a proposed contribution as already performed.

For organization work, [OCE.3](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce3---generate-and-compare-organization-concepts) supplies concept alternatives, [OCE.4](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce4---design-an-organizations-contribution-architecture) the contribution architecture, [OCE.7](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce7---coordinate-product-or-service-and-organization-architecture-decisions) paired product and organization decisions, and [OCE.9](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce9---realize-a-bounded-organization-capability-increment) bounded realization. Research Method Practice supplies the required inquiry; Human Capability Development, a selected human development programme; Community Management, a participation or common-work arrangement; and Implementation Facilitation, a helping undertaking. The [constituent table](#managementreference2---constituent-fields-and-their-contributions) and [external-contribution account](#managementreference6---boundaries-and-external-contributions) locate their full languages. C.32.MWA.PP connects the performance and provision arrangements, STR.16 tests joint feasibility where shared means make it a real question, and Leadership obtains missing joint contributions to formulation and enactment.

For example, a strategy may select an assisted diagnostic service while an organization design assumes every recipient will perform the diagnosis independently. The two texts describe different receiving results. If the service remains assisted, its plan must retain the qualified helper's actual contribution and demand. If independent mastery is selected, the capability and conditions for independent performance need their own grounds. Capability development is an additional result only where that capability is missing. A delivery plan remains infeasible if it relies on the same specialist for incompatible simultaneous demands, even when all its documents use the same role name. C.32.MWA.PP and STR.8 expose the first mismatch; STR.16 and LDR.2 carry any changed demand into a feasible agreed whole.

The resulting documents must agree about the subjects, commitments, means and contributions on which they rely. A provider's planned service, work actually delivered and a recipient's new capability remain separate claims. Assistance to a client stays within the agreed remit; scientific choice retains its independent criteria. An affected change returns to each decision or receiving use that depended on the old condition, while independently adequate results remain usable.

Only the content needed for the next responsible action is required. A recurrent local practice can warrant an LPF under E.4.DPF, as C.40.OD:4.8 explains; a contract, resource allocation or project document does not acquire that function by being placed beside it. If a required construction is absent from the supplying Methods, the remaining result is the specific missing Method or connection, not a complete package established by its document titles.

## Management.Reference:5 - Connected uses

### Management.Reference:5.1 - A voluntary practice-development network

Several independent groups want to develop and exchange a better diagnostic practice. Their useful result is a repertoire that practitioners can apply; their members also value mutual help. They are considering a shared development office, a small coordination service and separate provision by each group.

[STR.16](STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str16---construct-a-feasible-portfolio-with-shared-or-branch-specific-support) compares those arrangements over the same period while preserving the distinct inquiry and practitioner uses. [CB.14](COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb14---develop-and-maintain-a-shared-repertoire-of-practice) organises the joint work on the repertoire; [RMP](../RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) supplies a needed research result, and [FPF C.40.OD](../../FPF-Spec.md#c40od---construct-and-continue-open-ended-development) supplies the larger development construction when continuing development is the purpose. Management must make the chosen contribution supportable without deciding its scientific conclusion by agreement.

In this constructed situation, a qualified reviewer has eight available hours in the relevant week. Each of two proposed activities requires five of those hours, including preparation and return. Each fits alone; together they require ten. [MA.2](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma2---explain-the-cost-and-use-of-capacity) keeps the relevant capacity distinct from nominal availability, [CB.9](COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb9---provide-for-community-work-and-agree-its-terms) exposes the participants' other commitments and support terms, and [LDR.2](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldr2---agree-feasible-joint-contributions) constructs a feasible whole. A qualified external contribution, different timing or a smaller promise can resolve the shortage. Shared administration alone supplies none of the missing review hours.

[CB.13](COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb13---establish-a-workable-mandate-for-shared-decisions) establishes who may make the common allocation, where a mandate is missing. Each group retains the powers and commitments it has not delegated. [LDR.4](LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ldr4---prepare-a-proposal-for-decision-and-first-use) helps carry the chosen proposal into effective decisions and first use. Existing adequate access and arrangements can be retained; [ADM.9](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm9---provide-a-usable-administrative-result) supplies a missing administrative condition. A no-office arrangement can be sufficient. Help from a qualified person or AI can supply a contribution without requiring every participant to learn its Method; consent, information permissions and the actual means to rely on that help remain conditions.

If a volunteer withdraws an offered contribution, the management question is which promises depend on it and what can now be agreed. The available research findings remain available within their grounds. [CB.11](COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb11---continue-change-transfer-or-end-a-community-arrangement) can support reduction, transfer or ending if no feasible continuation remains. This preserves voluntary participation while making the common undertaking dependable within its stated limits.

### Management.Reference:5.2 - A new order in an operating business

The constructed order in [MA.1](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma1---build-the-resource-consumption-and-cost-model) requires 26–29 rig-hours for 100 accepted units. Twenty usable hours and a purchasable ten-hour block supply enough capacity under the case's conditions. The block can be booked for 240 currency units; other additional payments are 300. [OPS.14](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops14---relate-throughput-cash-and-operating-consequences) compares the 1,200 receipt with 540 of additional payments, giving 660 under the stated absence of displaced work.

That positive difference leaves the dated funding question open. Without the order, the associated example supplies 500 of unrestricted cash through day 28 after all other receipts and obligations. The order requires 440 now, leaving 60; another 100 is due on day 7, while its receipt arrives on day 28. The day-7 funding gap is therefore 40. [FIN.2](CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin2---assess-liquidity-and-funding-needs-by-date) is the entry when that corporate liquidity question needs further construction. The responsible participants can obtain funding, agree changed payment terms, revise timing or refuse the proposed order; the favorable total does not select the response.

[MKT.11](MARKETING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mkt11---align-promises-partners-and-execution) makes the offered delivery conditions match the supported arrangement, and [OPS.13](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops13---align-commitments-resources-and-service-outcomes) preserves the obligations already made to other customers. [ADM.8](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm8---establish-and-exercise-the-required-permission-for-an-administrative-action) and [ADM.9](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm9---provide-a-usable-administrative-result) obtain any missing permission and usable provision. Use [CGOV.3](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov3---establish-authority-for-corporate-appointments-removals-and-decisions) and [CGOV.11](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov11---make-and-record-a-corporate-decision) if the proposed act exceeds an existing delegation or requires a corporate decision. Ordinary work within an adequate delegation can continue directly.

If the choice instead turns on keeping, leasing or replacing the rig, [EAM.10](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam10---compare-engineered-asset-portfolio-combinations) and [EAM.12](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam12---integrate-specialist-results-for-an-asset-recommendation-or-decision) add the asset comparison and its qualified technical inputs. Engineering supplies the needed design or functioning result. Management selects and supports the contribution and follows what it actually makes possible in the service. The calculation illustrates the joins; real capacity, terms, safety and authority require the evidence applicable to the actual order.

### Management.Reference:5.3 - An AI-assisted experimental research programme

A laboratory is considering AI-assisted research on an enzyme. It could seek a useful variant with a specified property, a better predictive model or an explanation of a mechanism. Those are different results: finding a good variant need not distinguish two explanations of why it works. RMP.2 constructs the inquiry appropriate to the intended claim; STR.7 asks whether obtaining that knowledge warrants the resources and delay. Management must preserve that distinction when agreeing the programme's result.

Suppose the immediate commitment is a bounded search for variants that retain a required activity after a specified treatment. The assay, admissible variation, uncertainty and independent confirmation must come from qualified research and engineering work. OCE.8 compares complete available arrangements: a scientist using existing tools, a specialist optimizer connected to laboratory automation, an LLM with scientific tools, and a mixed arrangement. It includes preparation, failed attempts, laboratory time, checking and interpretation. Adding AI to existing job descriptions is only one candidate. OCE.3 constructs other divisions of the work; LDR.2 obtains feasible contributions rather than assuming that an organization chart supplies them.

The distinction is supported by two different research lines. [Co-Scientist, Gottweis and colleagues, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10644-y), develops hypotheses through generation, criticism, ranking and revision, with scientists and separate experimental validation. A hypothesis's ranking is not experimental evidence for its truth. [SAMPLE, Rapp and colleagues, 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s44286-023-00002-4), instead demonstrates a specialized model–experiment loop for a bounded protein search. It models functionality as well as the property being optimized. These are candidates for different contributions, not two interchangeable demonstrations that an autonomous laboratory is generally superior.

Here is a constructed capacity example, not a report of either study. A week's provision permits twelve assay slots. The chosen protocol requires two control slots and reserves two for independent confirmation, leaving eight for exploratory trials. Raising candidate generation from twenty to eighty variants does not create another assay slot. MMP.16 supplies the comparison of obtainable observations and their value for the selected unknown; RMP.3 makes the chosen design executable. OPS.9 and OPS.18 relate that design to the shared bench and other commitments. The next useful commitment may be eight selected trials, a different experimental design, extra qualified capacity or a decision not to proceed. The counts alone do not select among them.

Different returns reopen different contributions. If a dispensing failure prevents one assay, RMP.4 preserves the failed execution and its conditions; the optimizer must not receive an invented zero-activity measurement. The bench arrangement is repaired or the run is repeated when warranted. If a valid assay falls below the activity threshold, it is evidence about that variant under those conditions, not by itself a refutation of a wider mechanism. If an attractive scalar score conflicts with the raw observations, RMP.6 and the measurement construction must resolve whether the observation is unusable, the transformation is inappropriate or the model needs revision. An unusual signal cannot be discarded merely because it disagrees with the current model.

That last distinction matters in autonomous search. [Harris and colleagues, 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-024-01485-2), show how checking raw observations and their reduction to a scalar can change the next experiment selected by Bayesian optimization. Their synthetic and surrogate-data comparisons support a design alternative for oversight, not a demonstrated improvement of this laboratory. A qualified observer, its access to raw data and its consequences for the next proposal belong in the complete arrangement being compared.

The chosen workflow therefore connects hypothesis or candidate proposal, experiment selection, physically obtainable execution, interpretation of the actual return, model or claim revision, and separate confirmation. SYSE.47 constructs a tool-using procedure where automation is needed; SYSE.46 tests the complete configuration under representative conditions. A protocol that can call an instrument still needs the instrument's qualified behavior and the authority to use it. ADM.8 applies an adequate existing permission or obtains a missing one; it does not supply scientific validity. STR.7 and the responsible management decision then use the qualified research return to continue, change or stop the commitment.

This case explains why the Suite connects these management contributions and receives research, mathematical and engineering results without absorbing their disciplines. It does not provide an assay or a universal laboratory Method. A usable local arrangement still needs the complete supplying Methods, its domain models and explicit treatment of each consequential return. A successful variant, a better model and an explained mechanism remain separately warranted achievements.

## Management.Reference:6 - Boundaries and external contributions

| Needed contribution | Supplying practice and return |
| --- | --- |
| Maintain required functioning through policy, work and programme | [Maintenance Engineering and Management (MNT)](../Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md). How can required functioning be maintained through technically supported policy, feasible work and a continuing programme? [MNT.2](../Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt2---select-and-reopen-the-maintenance-policy), [MNT.7](../Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt7---coordinate-maintenance-intervention-and-continuing-operation) and [MNT.13](../Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt13---coordinate-the-maintenance-programme-and-fleet-learning) connect policy, operation and programme learning. Failure and condition knowledge constrain service promises, response and support. Programme evidence can change the policy, provision or operating commitment while asset-value decisions remain with EAM. |
| Engineer a product, service or platform | [Engineering](../Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/) supplies the relevant design, realization and qualification Methods. Management supplies purpose, commitments and provision and uses the qualified result. The practitioner may perform the engineering Method or obtain its result, according to capability and authority. OCE's organizational construction is already a constituent described in section 3.1; a management act can also change the undertaking's current Work or resource conditions without requiring a new product or platform design. |
| Develop a person's capability | [Human Capability Engineering](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/), including [Human Capability Development (HCD)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md), supplies human learning, practice and capability evidence. Management provides a receiving work need and feasible conditions when it relies on that capability. Assignment or attendance alone leaves the capability question open. A person supplying coaching and a manager arranging collective Work can have different direct subjects even when they support the same team. |
| Construct models or investigate a difficult choice | [Decision Design (PSDA)](../DECISION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) supplies formulations, representations and warranted comparisons. [Foundational Thinking](../Foundational%20Thinking%20DPF%20Suite/) supplies its formal and model-building contributions. A management use receives the relevant result under its conditions; these fields also serve other purposes. |
| Obtain professional decision support | [Decision Design’s professional-support Methods (PSDA)](../DECISION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) supply engagement, representation, protected participation and advice. The receiving management decision retains its authority and implementation duties. |
| Obtain new knowledge or a usable explanation | [Research Method Practice (RMP)](../RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) supplies criticism-bearing inquiry; [Explanation Design (EXD)](../EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) supplies an account the intended recipient can recover and use. The management need selects the required contribution without supplying its epistemic grounds. |
| Obtain help in applying a practice | [Implementation Facilitation (IS)](../IMPLEMENTATION-FACILITATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) supplies suitable assistance and its continuation or stop. Management can procure or allocate this help. Successful application alone establishes neither acquired capability nor open-ended development. |
| Continue development beyond one successful application | [FPF C.40.OD](../../FPF-Spec.md#c40od---construct-and-continue-open-ended-development) constructs open-ended development; [FPF C.40.JD](../../FPF-Spec.md#c40jd---develop-a-way-its-holder-and-its-provision-together) connects a way, its holder and provision; [FPF C.40.NP](../../FPF-Spec.md#c40np---continue-from-a-result-to-new-attainable-problems) continues from a result to another worthwhile attainable problem. Management can support such work while its development result remains separately judged. |

These rows identify useful supplies outside the constituent assembly described in section 2. Using another field's full Method, whether performed by the manager or by a specialist, retains the field's own subject and conditions. In particular, maintenance policy and programme work remain available without making the complete MNT field a Management constituent. OCE's organizational construction belongs to the constituent assembly for the subject reasons in section 3.1. The general construction of opportunities, composition of Methods and choice under constraints remains in FPF Core.

Management could participate in a broader discipline concerned with organising and changing collective activity, connecting its engineering contributions to wider system engineering and inquiry into social institutions and behaviour. It would contribute knowledge and practices for justified direction, legitimate commitments, provision and accountable continuation. It would receive qualified accounts of system capability and of the social conditions that affect those commitments. The broader assembly would need to connect a worthwhile collective result to both technically realizable and institutionally supportable action, and return failed premises to the corresponding practice. Management would retain its subject and the joint-supportability characteristic described above; engineering qualification and the grounds of social inquiry would remain with their respective disciplines. This is a possible assembly whose own field construction must be established before claiming that these disciplines are its parts.

## Management.Reference:7 - Continuity and coverage

Management retains its disciplinary identity while its theories, tools, techniques and institutional forms change, provided that its subject and essential knowledge–practice connections remain: direction and commitments are related to legitimate acts, obtainable means, actual performance and warranted reconsideration. An adequate replacement for a constituent method must preserve the contribution on which the remaining work relies. For example, a different forecasting method can replace one used in an operating promise if its population, capacity conditions, uncertainty and receiving use remain adequately supported.

For OCE, a replacement organization model or Method preserves its constituent contribution here when organizational knowledge remains connected to constructed relations, capability, commitments and their observed consequences. For an MNT contribution used here, a replacement policy or technology must preserve the connection between required functioning, supported technical reasoning, feasible provision and feedback to the programme. Both retain their engineering conditions. A change to one assignment, machine or service condition reopens the affected uses. Extending maintenance to all organizational change or to asset-value decisions would change its bounded subject.

An account that removes authority from the commitment question, separates resource knowledge from the work it explains, or replaces voluntary participation with an assumed right to assign people loses an essential connection of the management field described here. Extending coverage to another management branch can preserve that whole when its distinct subject, contributions and consequential connections are established.

This edition offers a connected selection of management fields. Marketing develops the customer-situation and feasible-offer branch; CUST develops the relation between client variation, repeatable offerings and their continuing obligations; Finance and Governance retain their corporate scope. The Suite does not provide complete coverage of organizational behavior, employment and human-resource management, public administration, international management or supply-chain management. Obtain the appropriate professional contribution when a task depends on those subjects. The boundaries of each included DPF remain applicable.

Each constituent retains its own sources, cases and conditions for reconsideration. New knowledge, a changed institutional condition or a revised Method reopens the other contributions that rely on it. Preserve independently adequate knowledge and practices while correcting the affected connection.

## Management.Reference:8 - Field basis and further reading

### Management.Reference:8.1 - Recognition of the field and its boundaries


Management is a recognized field of scholarship and practice with differentiated intellectual traditions. The Academy of Management's [divisions and interest groups](https://www.aom.org/divisions-and-interest-groups/) provide an institutional entry to that diversity. The Suite's particular composition is argued through its constituent subjects and working connections above.

The [Strategic Management domain statement](https://www.aom.org/divisions-and-interest-groups/strategic-management/) connects knowledge of organizational strategy with decision processes, resources and consequences. [Organization and Management Theory](https://www.aom.org/divisions-and-interest-groups/organization-and-management-theory/) studies organizations, organizing and their wider relations, joining theoretical inquiry with practical implications. [Operations and Supply Chain Management](https://www.aom.org/divisions-and-interest-groups/operations-and-supply-chain-management/) explicitly includes transformation processes in profit and nonprofit organizations and encourages connections across functions. These statements support recognition of the field and its breadth. They do not determine the membership of this Suite or validate a particular method.

The organization-change field has a constructive management basis in [Galbraith's organization-design practice](https://jaygalbraith.com/services/organization-design/) and an engineering connection explained by [SEBoK's Enterprise Systems Engineering account](https://sebokwiki.org/wiki/Enterprise_Systems_Engineering). The [AOM Organization Development and Change domain](https://www.aom.org/Divisions-and-Interest-Groups/Organization-Development-and-Change/) is broader than OCE's deliberate changes to organizational relations and capability. Those sources support related practices and their boundaries, not an equation of their complete subjects.

In §2, the [GFMAM Maintenance Framework, second edition](https://www.gfmam.org/sites/default/files/2021-02/GFMAM%20Maintenance%20Framework%20-%202nd%20Edition%20Final.pdf) distinguishes maintenance engineering from maintenance management; §§6.4–6.9 connect strategy, resources, work, performance, information and programme. This connection supports keeping the bounded maintenance field complete when Management uses it. It does not make maintenance identical to all Asset Management.

The full DPFs carry the disciplinary sources and limits needed for their own Methods. [FPF C.20](../../FPF-Spec.md#c20---composition-of-udiscipline-discipline-cal) explains discipline composition; [FPF E.4.PFAD](../../FPF-Spec.md#e4pfad---principle-framework-architecture-decision) distinguishes that question from the choice of a framework or publication arrangement.

### Management.Reference:8.2 - Contemporary comparisons that change the management question

The field descriptions above do not settle how to organize work with current AI. For that question, compare actual arrangements and the results they obtain. The following primary sources expose alternatives and conditions that matter to the Suite's architecture; the full Methods retain their own detailed grounds.

| Management question | Evidence and its limits | Consequence for using the Methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Does faster coding produce more useful completed work? | [Cui and colleagues, published 2026](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mnsc.2025.00535), report randomized access to a coding assistant across three companies and increased completed tasks, measured principally through pull requests. This is positive evidence for the tested assistance, not for every current agent arrangement or the whole product result. [METR's February 2026 update](https://metr.org/blog/2026-02-24-uplift-update/) explains why selection of participants and tasks, parallel work and changed task content prevent its newer estimates from establishing a reliable current effect. | OCE.8 compares whole ways of obtaining a result; OPS.9, OPS.16 and OPS.22 follow the resulting flow, shared resources and consequences. Distinguish performance on comparable tasks from the value of a changed portfolio of tasks. A count of generated changes answers neither question alone. |
| Is checking necessarily going to consume the gain? | [Chen and Stratton, 2026 working paper](https://fion.ac/jellyfish.pdf), find that checking and rework can limit the conversion of more code into output following AI-agent adoption in observations across 718 firms. [He and colleagues, 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.01904v1), report a positive contrast in one company: authored pull requests per active developer reached 2.09 times the January–April 2025 baseline in April 2026, alongside increased review work. This is an observed ratio, not an estimated causal multiplier of AI. Both are observational; merge and revert measures do not settle long-term maintainability or customer value. | Retain both possibilities. OPS.9 examines the actual limiting contribution; OPS.22 asks what the measured change warrants. More generation can require a different allocation of checking effort, but a universal claim that review erases the gain is unwarranted. |
| Could another division of work be better than equipping the present team? | [The Cybernetic Teammate, published 2026](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/orsc.2025.20702), studies 791 P&G professionals in one day of early product-development tasks. Individuals with AI could match teams without AI in the quality of proposals, and AI users produced more balanced technical and commercial proposals. This does not establish the performance of a continuing department or a released physical product. | Include a specialist with AI, a differently constituted team and the existing arrangement among OCE.3 and OCE.8 alternatives. SYSE.44 supplies the engineering of agent work and its integration. Determine which expertise remains necessary for generation, selection, integration and the final judgement. |
| Can software-agent results be transferred to engineering hardware? | [Phoenix-bench, 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.15226v1), examines RTL tasks with signal hierarchy, related changes and executable EDA checks. Its selected repository tasks stop short of complete physical realization. It supplies a counterexample to treating a coding result as evidence for hardware development in general. | OCE.7 joins organizational and product conditions; SYSE.15 and SYSE.20 construct feasible engineering work and iterations. Compare the flow of variants and checks, including qualified models, test benches and irreversible acts. Faster proposals matter only through the result those contributions can qualify. |
| What can an earlier aerospace success explain? | The participants' [COTS Lessons Learned, 2013](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20150009324/downloads/20150009324.pdf), describe rapid iteration, early hardware and asynchronous review alongside retained safety requirements, interfaces, additional tests and NASA participation. This is a historical account of mechanisms, not a causal ranking of NASA and SpaceX or evidence for AI engineering. | Preserve the useful construction: change an obstructing dependency while retaining the evidence required by the receiving use. SYSE.20 supplies that reasoning. Choosing an organizational label or removing a review without examining its contribution does not reproduce the reported result. |
| How does a management mandate become an executable delegation? | [South and colleagues, ICML 2025](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/south25a.html), propose authenticated delegation using established authorization protocols. This is a technical construction and position, not an empirical proof of superior management. | ADM.8 and LDR.2 supply the applicable mandate and agreement. Where execution crosses agents or systems, obtain engineering that binds the permitted act to authenticated identity, bounded authority and revocation. A statement that an agent has a role does not implement that boundary. A sufficient local arrangement needs no extra delegation machinery. |

For AI-assisted research, the distinct hypotheses, experimental search and observation-quality lines in section 5.3 explain why scientific claims remain qualified by research and domain Methods. No institutional description, benchmark or individual company case validates the whole management arrangement.

### Management.Reference:8.3 - What the comparison establishes

The synthesis favors comparing complete applicable arrangements over importing a fixed organization form. It preserves more than one scale of judgement: the quality and cost of a particular contribution, the supportable flow of work, the resulting commitment, and its value in use. New capabilities can change the work worth attempting; STR.17 reopens the strategic question when a local efficiency comparison no longer represents that change.

For example, when AI changes which tasks are attempted and several agents share reviewers or laboratory equipment, a time-per-task comparison is insufficient. A useful comparison must keep the original needs and declined work visible, distinguish comparable tasks from the changed undertaking, account for shared resources and retain checking and subsequent losses. Its design needs the relevant measurement and causal-inference expertise. An observed improvement, a locally useful arrangement and an established causal effect are different conclusions. Neither this Reference nor a positive study supplies that design for every undertaking.

The older source is retained where its construction remains adequate; a newer source reopens the affected decision when it supplies a better alternative or defeats a premise. Conversely, a new date, a leading company's name or institutional endorsement is not a sufficient selection rule. Reconsider the arrangement when its result, task mix, technology, limiting resource, authority or consequential horizon changes. These comparisons justify specific questions and alternatives; they do not assign a single state-of-the-art rank to every Method in the Suite.

## Management.Reference:End
